GLASSBOX-MEGAJAM-2026 lane=props1

You are the compile lane on SUPERCUT, a first-person jam game in Unreal Engine 5.9 (C++, no Blueprints, rooms built by code from text room files). Your job: put twelve finished prop meshes into the game as set dressing. You are the only lane allowed to change the game repo right now. Do the work yourself, start no subagents.

## The look, so you place things with sense
The whole game is a film director's tabletop model of a set, at 1:25: foam board and card walls on a green cutting mat, lit by one desk lamp, in a dark studio. The player is a figure inside the model. When the player claps the clapperboard time freezes and the picture becomes a pencil storyboard drawing (a screen effect that reads a "sketch" mark on each mesh). The props come in two kinds:
- **Desk things at real desk size, so giant to the player** (they give the scale away): desk lamp, steel ruler, pencil, glue bottle, masking tape roll, set square.
- **Model film gear at the player's size** (card and balsa models, part of the set): director's chair, film light on a stand, film camera on a tripod, apple boxes, sandbags, cable reel.

## The files (all checked and approved by the owner; do not edit the meshes)
- `[notes]\unreal\megajam-2026\lanes\rodin2\out\`: `SM_SteelRuler`, `SM_Pencil`, `SM_GlueBottle`, `SM_MaskingTape`, `SM_SetSquare`, `SM_FilmLight`, `SM_FilmCamera`, `SM_AppleBoxes`, `SM_Sandbags`, `SM_CableReel` (`.fbx`), each with `T_<Name>_BC.png` (1024).
- `[notes]\unreal\megajam-2026\lanes\rodin1\out\`: `SM_Lamp_CODEX.fbx` + `T_Lamp_CODEX_BC.png` (2048), `SM_DirectorChair_CODEX.fbx` + `T_DirectorChair_CODEX_BC.png`. Import these two as `SM_Lamp` and `SM_DirectorChair`. **Do not import `SM_CraftKnife_CODEX`** (the owner rejected it; a new knife comes later).
- Facts: centimetres at the player's scale, use at scale 1; FBX written by Blender with its default axes (-Z forward, Y up), so check which way is up after import; pivot at base centre; one mesh, one material, base colour only; 3,000 triangles each, the lamp 8,000. Sizes and known small defects: `lanes\rodin2\HANDOFF.md` (table near line 20) and `lanes\rodin1\HANDOFF.md` (section "Mesh facts for the import"). Lamp 1125 cm tall, ruler 800 cm long, pencil 400, glue bottle 375 tall, tape 225 across, set square 625; film light 200 tall, camera 170, chair 86, apple boxes 51, sandbags 60, cable reel 50.
- A later knife will arrive as `lanes\rodin3\out\SM_CraftKnife.fbx` (400 cm long, lies flat). Build the import so adding it is one entry in a list plus one placement line, and write the exact steps in your HANDOFF.

## What to build
1. **Import.** Copy the 12 FBX and 12 textures into the game repo under `Art\props_gen\` (with a short `SOURCE.md`: made for this game on 14 Nov 2026 with Codex image generation, Hyper3D Rodin and Blender clean-up; lanes rodin1 and rodin2). Import them into `Content\Props\` through the project's asset script the way the other meshes and textures get in (`Tools\make_assets.py`, `Tools\make_figures.py`; it needs `-AllowCommandletRendering`, see GOTCHAS). No Nanite. Texture settings that suit a base colour map. One material that takes a base colour texture and fits the game's maquette materials (read how `make_maquette` and `SupercutShapes` build and mark materials; do not invent a second system). Every prop must carry the right sketch mark so it draws correctly in a freeze: check how `SupercutShapes::MarkForSketch` and its `ESketch` values are used and pick the fitting one for model pieces and for studio pieces.
2. **The lamp.** Every room already gets one lamp light from `ASupercutRoom::BuildLight` (`Source\Supercut\SupercutRoom.cpp`), with a glowing shade part. Put the lamp mesh there so it reads as the lamp that light comes from: head at the light, turned the way the light points, base standing on the desk outside the model's walls. You may scale the lamp uniformly to make that fit, and you may drop or shrink the old shade part if the mesh now does its job, but the light itself (position, strength, cone, colour) must not change by one number. The lamp face has no glow in its texture: keep some glowing part at the bulb so the head reads as lit.
3. **Desk things.** Lay the ruler, pencil, glue bottle, tape roll and set square on the desk outside the room's walls, where the player can see at least one or two of them over or past the walls from normal play positions. No collision. Not every room needs every tool; vary which ones and where so eight rooms do not look stamped. They must not sit inside a room, block a door, or poke through a wall.
4. **Film gear.** Put chair, film light, camera, apple boxes, sandbags and cable reel inside rooms at the edges: corners, against walls, beside doorways, grouped the way a crew would leave them (light on its stand with a sandbag on its foot, camera with apple boxes beside it, chair near the camera). Two to five pieces per room. They block the player (simple box collision) but must sit clear of every walk path, enemy home area, shot line, door, blade, lava gap and pickup, and clear of the route the scripted run takes.
5. **How placement is written down.** Prefer lines in the room files (a new piece kind such as `prop <Name> x y z yaw [scale]`) so a person can move a prop by editing text, parsed where the other pieces are parsed (`SupercutRoomFile.cpp`, `SupercutRoomPieces.cpp`). An unknown prop name or a missing mesh must fail loudly with a clear error, the way the project's `LoadOrDie` does. No fallbacks. Add tests in the style of the existing test files for: the new line parses, a bad name fails, every room file's props load.
The placements are your call: use judgement, look at your own pictures, and fix what looks wrong. List every placement choice a person might disagree with in HANDOFF.md under "Taste calls", each with a picture.

## Must not change
- Gameplay. The scripted full run must print exactly `RUN wrapped: takes 1, time 98.2 s, shots 46, freezes 14, kills 17` on both packages:
  `powershell -File Tools\run_demo.ps1 -Packaged -Run main8 -Seed 1 -Script "D:\UE\Projects\Supercut59\Script\main8.txt" -FixedFps 240 -Silent -Log <file>` and the same with `-Shipping` in place of `-Packaged` (Shipping writes a log only through this `-Log`/`-SupercutLog=`). If a prop changes that line, move the prop; do not touch the script.
- The held items: the player's hands, revolver and clapperboard, their positions, the muzzle flash. Leave all of it alone.
- The light numbers, the sketch effect's look, sounds, menus, tuning defaults.
- Frame time. Before you change anything, and again at the end, run the same room walk on this PC with the Development package and log average and slowest-1% frame time with the game's own counter (`-SupercutFps`, already passed by the runner; without `-FixedFps` for this measurement). Report both. More than 5 percent slower at the end means something is wrong (a texture or mesh setting): find it. Do not run anything on the worker PCs; another lane is recording there.

## Rules
- This PC is used by a person. Send no real keyboard or mouse input, do not run `Tools\input_check.ps1`, play no sound aloud (`-Silent` on every run). One game at a time, windowed. Another lane runs short games here from its own build copy; before each build, package or game start read free memory (`powershell -NoProfile -Command "(Get-CimInstance Win32_OperatingSystem).FreePhysicalMemory/1MB"`) and wait while it is under 3 GB. Do not print user or account names, computer names or emails: no `ls -l`, `ls -la`, `dir /q`, `whoami`, `hostname`, no listing of `C:\Users`. For a file's time use `stat -c "%y" <file>`. ## Done means

## Packaging (BuildCookRun)

Verified 12 Nov 2026 on c4, engine 5.8.4, no Visual Studio installed.

- **Enabling Unreal MCP for every target turns a Blueprint-only project into a code project.**
  UAT prints "has no code, but is being treated as a code-based project ... because:
  ModelContextProtocol plugin is enabled", and then needs a compiler. Fix: give
  `ModelContextProtocol` and `AllToolsets` `"TargetAllowList": ["Editor"]` in the `.uproject`.
  UAT then prints "no longer being treated as a code-based project".
- **A content-only project is packaged without `-build` and without `-target=`.** With
  `-target=UnrealGame`: "Unable to find target 'UnrealGame'". With `-build` and no target:
  "does not look like uproject file but no targets have been found!". The reason is in
  `AutomationUtils/ProjectParams.cs`: with `-build`, UAT wants a `.Target.cs` inside the project.
- **A `"Modules"` key in the `.uproject` makes it a code project, even as `"Modules": []`.** UAT
  tests for the literal text (`ProjectUtils.cs`: `uprojectStr.Contains("\"Modules\"")`). Staging then
  fails with "Missing receipt '...\Binaries\Win64\<Name>.target'". The engine's own `TP_BlankBP`
  template carries the empty key. Delete the line.
- **`AllToolsets` breaks the cook.** It pulls in `GameFeaturesToolset`, which enables Game Features,
  which logs "Asset manager settings do not include a rule for assets of type GameFeatureData" as an
  Error, and any Error fails the cook ("Failure - 2 error(s)"). Enable the toolset plugins one by one
  and leave `GameFeaturesToolset` out. The list we use is in `FINDINGS.md`.
- **The archive includes `UnrealGame.pdb`, 280 MB.** Leave it out of the submission zip.
- **An empty Development build is 394 MB zipped.** The jam cap is 1 GB.
- The working command line and `.uproject` are in `FINDINGS.md`.

  at login, earlier than `AGameModeBase::StartPlay`. A camera pawn that read the town's size from

- **Canvas text with a Slate font draws nothing unless the font info holds a `UFont`.**
  `FCanvasTextItem` built from `FSlateFontInfo` checks `FontObject != nullptr`.
  `FCoreStyle::GetDefaultFontStyle` has no font object, so every string was silently skipped. Use
  `FSlateFontInfo(GEngine->GetMediumFont(), Size, FName("Bold"))` (Roboto, typeface names `Bold`,
  `Regular`).

# SUPERCUT lane light1: handoff

14 Nov 2026, c4, engine 5.9. Light pass, glow colours, two code fixes.

## Commit

- Game repo `D:\UE\Projects\Supercut59`, branch `ue59`: `edb423d` (parent `3583521`). Not pushed.

  `unreal\GOTCHAS.md` are in the working tree.

## What changed in the picture

**A. The lamp.** Every room is lit by one warm spot light with soft shadows. It stands high, behind the start and
to its left. A weak cool light with no shadows comes from the other side, so shadow sides stay readable. The walls
now run from cream white on the lamp side to grey on the shadow side. The mat is a deeper green and its grid still
reads. Round the model is a dark studio: a warm dark grey just above the walls that fades to black upward.

- One rule places everything: `ASupercutRoom::BuildLight` reads the box round the room's solid shapes and puts the
  lamp, the fill and the studio walls from it. No room file changed.

- The warm and cool `lamp` lines of room files are off (`RoomLampScale 0`). The red and green ones are halved
  (`AccentLampScale 0.5`), because the green one lit the wall by the gate to about 90 percent on its own.
- Exposure is fixed. `ExposureBias` and `BloomStrength` are tuning fields.

**B. Glow colours.** Danger, the player's shot and the open gate each take their hue from one tuning field. The
cores are kept at strength 1.5 to 2, where the tonemapper keeps the hue. The soft glow round a shot, the Grunt's
warning and the Marksman's line is a see-through shell of the same colour (new material `M_Halo`). The shell is not
drawn in frozen time.

**C. Frozen picture.** The dark studio has its own sketch value and draws as medium hatching. Before, it was dense
black scribble. Shadow sides of walls and flats get light hatching. Lit walls stay bare paper.

**D. Fixes.** The shot direction and the walk heading come from the control rotation, so a camera kick moves
neither. The crosshair has a dark edge under each of its five marks, like the hit marker.

#include "CoreMinimal.h"

class ASupercutRoom;

/** Builds one piece into a room that is being put together. A piece type's Read function returns one. */
using FSupercutPieceBuild = TFunction<void(ASupercutRoom&)>;

/**
 * A fact one line of a room file states for the whole-room checks, such as "door a is here" or
 * "this line needs door a". A piece type writes it with FSupercutPieceReader::Note.
 */
struct FSupercutRoomNote
{
	FString Key;      // what kind of fact: "door", "door user", "glyph", ...
	FString Value;
	int32 Number = 0;
	FString Type;     // the piece type of the line
	int32 Line = 0;
};

/**
 * One line of a room file while its settings are read.
 *
 * A piece type asks for each setting by name. A setting that is missing, a value that does not
 * parse and a setting nobody asked for all become errors that name the file and the line.
 * Nothing is ever filled in with a default.
 */

	bool YesNo(const TCHAR* Key);          // yes or no

	bool Has(const TCHAR* Key) const { return Settings.Contains(Key); }

	void FailUnreadSettings();

# Finds the lamp's shade opening from the texture: the inside of the shade and the bulb are painted bright.
import sys
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image
sys.path.insert(0, sys.argv[1])
import fbxread
m = fbxread.mesh(sys.argv[2])
tex = np.asarray(Image.open(sys.argv[3]).convert("RGB")).astype(float) / 255
H, W, _ = tex.shape
v, pvi, uv, uvi = m["verts"], m["pvi"], m["uv"], m["uvi"]
idx = np.where(pvi < 0, ~pvi, pvi)
# per polygon-vertex: position, uv
P = v[idx]
UV = uv[uvi]
px = np.clip((UV[:, 0] % 1) * W, 0, W - 1).astype(int)
py = np.clip((1 - UV[:, 1] % 1) * H, 0, H - 1).astype(int)
lum = tex[py, px] @ np.array([0.299, 0.587, 0.114])
print("lum percentiles", np.round(np.percentile(lum, [50, 90, 95, 99, 99.9]), 3))
# polygons
ends = np.where(pvi < 0)[0]
starts = np.concatenate([[0], ends[:-1] + 1])
cent, nrm, plum, area = [], [], [], []
for s, e in zip(starts, ends):
    q = P[s:e + 1]
    c = q.mean(0)
    n = np.cross(q[1] - q[0], q[2] - q[0])
    a = np.linalg.norm(n) / 2
    cent.append(c); nrm.append(n / (2 * a + 1e-9)); plum.append(lum[s:e + 1].mean()); area.append(a)
cent, nrm, plum, area = map(np.array, (cent, nrm, plum, area))
for thr in (0.5, 0.6, 0.7):
    sel = plum > thr
    if sel.sum() == 0:
        continue
    w = area[sel]
    c = (cent[sel] * w[:, None]).sum(0) / w.sum()
    n = (nrm[sel] * w[:, None]).sum(0); n /= np.linalg.norm(n)
    print("thr %.1f polys %d area %.0f centre %s normal %s  bbox %s %s" % (thr, sel.sum(), w.sum(), np.round(c, 1), np.round(n, 3),
          np.round(cent[sel].min(0), 0), np.round(cent[sel].max(0), 0)))
# height profile: where is the top part (shade) in xy
top = cent[:, 2] > 800
print("z>800 centre", np.round(cent[top].mean(0), 1), "xy range", np.round(cent[top].min(0)), np.round(cent[top].max(0)))
base = cent[:, 2] < 100
print("z<100 centre", np.round(cent[base].mean(0), 1), "range", np.round(cent[base].min(0)), np.round(cent[base].max(0)))
EOF
python -I props1/tools/lamp_bulb.py "$(pwd)/props1/tools" rodin1/out/SM_Lamp_CODEX.fbx rodin1/out/T_Lamp_CODEX_BC.png

# Three orthographic point views of the lamp (side YZ, front XZ, top XY), bright-texture points in orange. Blender axes.
import sys
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw
sys.path.insert(0, sys.argv[1])
import fbxread
m = fbxread.mesh(sys.argv[2])
tex = np.asarray(Image.open(sys.argv[3]).convert("RGB")).astype(float) / 255
H, W, _ = tex.shape
v, pvi, uv, uvi = m["verts"], m["pvi"], m["uv"], m["uvi"]
idx = np.where(pvi < 0, ~pvi, pvi)
P = v[idx]; UV = uv[uvi]
px = np.clip((UV[:, 0] % 1) * W, 0, W - 1).astype(int); py = np.clip((1 - UV[:, 1] % 1) * H, 0, H - 1).astype(int)
C = tex[py, px]
lum = C @ np.array([0.299, 0.587, 0.114])
S = 0.4
img = Image.new("RGB", (int(3 * 1200 * S), int(1200 * S)), (255, 255, 255))
d = ImageDraw.Draw(img)
for k, (a, b) in enumerate(((1, 2), (0, 2), (0, 1))):
    ox = k * 1200 * S + 600 * S
    for p, c, l in zip(P, C, lum):
        x = ox + p[a] * S
        y = (1150 - p[b]) * S if b == 2 else 600 * S - p[b] * S
        col = (255, 120, 0) if l > 0.6 else tuple(int(t * 200) for t in c)
        d.point((x, y), fill=col)
    d.text((ox - 550 * S, 5), ["side: right=+Y, up=+Z", "front: right=+X, up=+Z", "top: right=+X, up=+Y"][k], fill=(0, 0, 0))
img.save(sys.argv[4])
EOF

# Shade axis of the lamp: sphere fit to the shade, then the axis that makes the shade's mouth a flat ring. Blender axes.
import sys
import numpy as np
sys.path.insert(0, sys.argv[1])
import fbxread
m = fbxread.mesh(sys.argv[2])
v = m["verts"]
shade = v[(v[:, 1] < -100) & (v[:, 2] > 640)]
A = np.c_[2 * shade, np.ones(len(shade))]
b = (shade ** 2).sum(1)
sol = np.linalg.lstsq(A, b, rcond=None)[0]
c = sol[:3]; r = np.sqrt(sol[3] + c @ c)
print("shade points", len(shade), "sphere centre", np.round(c, 1), "radius", round(r, 1))
best = None
for th in np.radians(np.arange(0, 91, 1)):
    for ph in np.radians(np.arange(-30, 31, 2)):
        a = np.array([np.sin(ph) * np.cos(th), -np.cos(ph) * np.cos(th), -np.sin(th)])
        t = (shade - c) @ a
        top = shade[t > np.percentile(t, 92)]
        # flatness of the mouth: spread of the top 8% along the axis, relative to radius
        spread = np.std((top - c) @ a)
        radial = np.linalg.norm((top - c) - np.outer((top - c) @ a, a), axis=1)
        score = spread / (radial.mean() + 1e-9)
        if best is None or score < best[0]:
            best = (score, np.degrees(th), np.degrees(ph), a, top.mean(0), radial.mean(), np.percentile(t, 100))
print("axis pitch down %.0f deg, sideways %.0f deg, dir %s, mouth centre %s, mouth radius %.0f, mouth at %.0f from centre" %
      (best[1], best[2], np.round(best[3], 3), np.round(best[4], 1), best[5], best[6]))
EOF

// (the film can registers itself in SupercutFilmCan.cpp, and a new piece type should do the same).
//
// Each block below is one piece type: the word that starts its line, how many a room may hold, and
// a function that reads the line's settings and returns the step that builds the piece.

#include "SupercutGrunt.h"
#include "SupercutMachines.h"
#include "SupercutRoom.h"
#include "SupercutRoomFile.h"

namespace
{
	/** Reads from= and to= as the two opposite corners of a box. from must be the lower corner on every axis. */
	FBox Corners(FSupercutPieceReader& In)
	{
		const FVector From = In.Vector(TEXT("from"));
		const FVector To = In.Vector(TEXT("to"));
		if (From.X >= To.X || From.Y >= To.Y || From.Z >= To.Z)
		{
			In.Fail(FString::Printf(TEXT("from=%.0f,%.0f,%.0f must be lower than to=%.0f,%.0f,%.0f on x, y and z"), From.X, From.Y, From.Z, To.X, To.Y, To.Z));
		}
		return FBox(From, To);
	}

	FString Role(FSupercutPieceReader& In)
	{
		const FString Word = In.Word(TEXT("role"));
		if (!Word.IsEmpty() && !ASupercutRoom::IsRole(Word))
		{
			In.Fail(FString::Printf(TEXT("role=%s is not a colour role. The roles are: %s"), *Word, *ASupercutRoom::RoleNames()));
		}
		return Word;
	}

	// Lamp colours by name, as colour roles are for boxes.
	struct FLampColor
	{
		const TCHAR* Name;
		FLinearColor Color;
		bool bAccent;   // a coloured lamp that marks a place, not one that lights the room
	};
	const FLampColor LampColors[] =
	{
		{ TEXT("warm"),  FLinearColor(1.0f, 0.9f, 0.75f), false },   // stage lamps
		{ TEXT("cool"),  FLinearColor(0.8f, 0.9f, 1.0f),  false },
		{ TEXT("red"),   FLinearColor(1.0f, 0.3f, 0.2f),  true },    // near a hazard
		{ TEXT("green"), FLinearColor(0.7f, 1.0f, 0.8f),  true },    // near the end gate
	};
}

// box role=wall from=x,y,z to=x,y,z
// A solid box: floor, wall, cover, ledge, step.
static FSupercutPieceType GBoxPiece(TEXT("box"), ESupercutPieceCount::Any, [](FSupercutPieceReader& In) -> FSupercutPieceBuild
{
	const FString Word = Role(In);
	const FBox Box = Corners(In);
	return [=](ASupercutRoom& Room) { Room.AddBox(Box.Min, Box.Max, Room.RoleMaterial(Word), true); };
});

void FSupercutPieceReader::Report(const FString& What)
{
	bSettingFailed = true;
	Errors.Add(FString::Printf(TEXT("%s: %s: %s"), *Where(File, Line), *Type, *What));

const FString* FSupercutPieceReader::Find(const TCHAR* Key)
{
	Asked.Add(Key);
	const FString* Value = Settings.Find(Key);
	if (!Value)
	{
		Report(FString::Printf(TEXT("the setting \"%s\" is missing"), Key));
	}
	return Value;
}

bool FSupercutPieceReader::Numbers(const TCHAR* Key, int32 Count, const TCHAR* Shape, double* Out)
{
	const FString* Value = Find(Key);
	if (!Value)
	{
		return false;
	}
	TArray<FString> Parts;
	Value->ParseIntoArray(Parts, TEXT(","), false);
	bool bGood = Parts.Num() == Count;
	for (int32 Index = 0; bGood && Index < Count; ++Index)
	{
		bGood = !Parts[Index].IsEmpty() && FCString::IsNumeric(*Parts[Index]);
		Out[Index] = bGood ? FCString::Atod(*Parts[Index]) : 0.0;
	}
	if (!bGood)
	{
		Report(FString::Printf(TEXT("%s=%s is not %s"), Key, **Value, Shape));
	}
	return bGood;
}

float FSupercutPieceReader::Number(const TCHAR* Key)
{
	double Value[1] = { 0.0 };
	Numbers(Key, 1, TEXT("a number"), Value);
	return float(Value[0]);
}

FVector FSupercutPieceReader::Vector(const TCHAR* Key)
{
	double Value[3] = { 0.0, 0.0, 0.0 };
	Numbers(Key, 3, TEXT("three numbers written x,y,z with no spaces"), Value);
	return FVector(Value[0], Value[1], Value[2]);
}

FVector2D FSupercutPieceReader::Point(const TCHAR* Key)
{
	double Value[2] = { 0.0, 0.0 };
	Numbers(Key, 2, TEXT("two numbers written x,y with no spaces"), Value);
	return FVector2D(Value[0], Value[1]);
}

FString FSupercutPieceReader::Word(const TCHAR* Key)
{
	const FString* Value = Find(Key);
	return Value ? Value->ToLower() : FString();
}

bool FSupercutPieceReader::YesNo(const TCHAR* Key)
{
	const FString* Value = Find(Key);
	if (!Value)
	{
		return false;
	}
	if (*Value != TEXT("yes") && *Value != TEXT("no"))
	{
		Report(FString::Printf(TEXT("%s=%s is not yes or no"), Key, **Value));
	}
	return *Value == TEXT("yes");
}

void FSupercutPieceReader::FailUnreadSettings()
{
	for (const TPair<FString, FString>& Setting : Settings)
	{
		if (!Asked.Contains(Setting.Key))
		{
			Report(FString::Printf(TEXT("has no setting called \"%s\""), *Setting.Key));
		}
	}
}

}

void ASupercutPlayerController::RunScript(float DeltaTime, FSupercutInput& Input, ASupercutCharacter* Hero, USupercutRun& Run)
{
	if (bScriptOver)
	{
		return;
	}

	if (Hero->IsDead() && !bDeathExpected)
	{
		FailScript(FString::Printf(TEXT("the player died (%s)"), *Hero->GetDeathCause()));
		return;
	}

	ScriptClock += DeltaTime;
	while (NextStep < Steps.Num() && Steps[NextStep].Time <= ScriptClock)
	{
		const FStep& Step = Steps[NextStep];
		if (Step.Command == TEXT("scene"))
		{
			if (Run.GetRoomEntries() == RoomEntriesSeen)
			{
				// Still in the old room, or on a screen between rooms. Wait here.
				SceneWait += DeltaTime;
				if (SceneWait > SceneWaitLimit)
				{
					FailScript(FString::Printf(TEXT("waited %.0f s at a \"scene\" line and the run did not enter a new room"), SceneWaitLimit));
					return;
				}
				break;
			}
			const int32 WantScene = Step.Args.IsValidIndex(0) ? FCString::Atoi(*Step.Args[0]) : 0;
			const int32 WantTake = Step.Args.IsValidIndex(1) ? FCString::Atoi(*Step.Args[1]) : Run.GetTake();
			if (WantScene != Run.GetScene() || WantTake != Run.GetTake())
			{
				FailScript(FString::Printf(TEXT("the script expected scene %d take %d and the run is in scene %d take %d"), WantScene, WantTake, Run.GetScene(), Run.GetTake()));
				return;
			}
			RoomEntriesSeen = Run.GetRoomEntries();
			UE_LOG(LogSupercut, Display, TEXT("SCRIPT scene %d take %d entered after %.2f s, clock set to 0"), Run.GetScene(), Run.GetTake(), ScriptClock);
			ScriptClock = 0.f;
			SceneWait = 0.f;
			HeldForward = 0.f;
			HeldRight = 0.f;
			bHeldFire = false;
			bDeathExpected = false;
			++NextStep;
			continue;
		}

		RunStep(Step, Input, Hero);
		++NextStep;
		if (bScriptOver)
		{
			return;
		}
	}
	Input.Forward = HeldForward;
	Input.Right = HeldRight;
	Input.bFire = Input.bFire || bHeldFire;
}

void ASupercutPlayerController::LookAt(const FVector& Point, ASupercutCharacter* Hero)
{
	SetControlRotation((Point - Hero->GetEyeLocation()).Rotation());
}

# Reads SM_Lamp's vertices after import and prints the centre of the vertices above 800 cm and of the shade
# region, to tell whether Blender's -Y became Unreal's +Y. Read only.
import unreal
mesh = unreal.load_asset("/Game/Props/Set/SM_Lamp")
desc = mesh.get_static_mesh_description(0)
n = desc.get_vertex_count()
sx = sy = sz = 0.0
k = 0
for i in range(n):
    p = desc.get_vertex_position(unreal.VertexID(i))
    if p.z > 800:
        sx += p.x; sy += p.y; sz += p.z; k += 1
unreal.log("PROPS1 lamp vertices %d, above 800 cm: %d, centre %.1f %.1f %.1f" % (n, k, sx / k, sy / k, sz / k))
EOF

# SCENE: THE WIND MACHINE. First room of the run. It teaches the clapperboard without a word.
# Idea: the wind machine fills the only doorway and cannot be passed in live time. A freeze stops it.
#       The first Grunt stands just past it, so the player meets it frozen, shoots, and sees the shots hang.
# Lengths are cm. x runs from the start to the gate, y is left (-) to right (+), z is up.
#
# Plan (1 char = 100 cm, x to the right, +y down the page):
#
#   y-800            +------------------------------+
#                    |      F2            LEDGE  G1 |
#   y-450 +--------+ |      F2          +-----------|
#         |        |M|      F2  cr                  |
#   y   0 | S  - - |=B=  .  .  .               GATE |
#         |        |M|  F1                          |
#   y+450 +--------+ |  F1     G0                   |
#                    |                              |
#   y+800            +------------------------------+
#         x0      900 1400                       3400
#
#   S start, B wind machine (blade) in the tunnel through the metal block M, F1 F2 flats, cr crate,
#   G0 Grunt 0 behind F1, G1 Grunt 1 on the ledge behind F2.

start    at=150,0,0 facing=0
gate     at=3150,0,0 facing=0
fall     below=-350
keylight pitch=-52 yaw=28 strength=4

box role=floor from=0,-850,-50       to=3450,850,0

# ---- Entry bay: x 0 to 900, y -450 to 450.
box role=wall  from=-50,-500,0       to=0,500,480
box role=wall  from=0,-500,0         to=900,-450,480
box role=wall  from=0,450,0          to=900,500,480

# ---- The wind machine's housing: a metal block 500 thick with a tunnel 340 wide and 420 high through it.
box role=metal from=900,-500,0       to=1400,-170,480
box role=metal from=900,170,0        to=1400,500,480
box role=metal from=900,-170,420     to=1400,170,480

# The blade: 220 deep, so at 1.5 turns a second nobody walks through between two sweeps
# (the bar passes every 0.33 s and the walk through its depth takes 0.49 s).
blade at=1150,0,210 facing=0 size=220,330,30 turns=1.5
mark role=danger from=1032,-170,0    to=1040,170,1.5
mark role=danger from=1260,-170,0    to=1268,170,1.5
lamp at=1150,0,380 color=red candelas=25 reach=900 shadows=yes

mark role=tape from=520,-5,0         to=620,5,1

4.87093734741211
# Builds one target of this project and survives the bad precompiled header trap.
# Usage: powershell -File Tools\build.ps1 [-Target SupercutEditor|Supercut] [-Engine D:\UE\UE_5.9] [-Jobs 1]
#
# The trap: on this PC the compiler sometimes writes a 2 GB+ shared precompiled header that is bad, with no
# error. Every file compiled against it then dies with "C1001 ... msc1.cpp, line 1589", and the build tool keeps
# reusing the bad header because it looks up to date. Seen on UE 5.8.4 and 5.9, with one job and with several.
# The only cure found is to delete the header and build it again. This script does that, up to 3 times, and
# says so each time. Any other failure is returned as it is.
param(
    [ValidateSet("SupercutEditor", "Supercut")] [string]$Target = "SupercutEditor",
    [string]$Engine = "D:\UE\UE_5.9",
    [int]$Jobs = 1
)
$proj = Split-Path -Parent $PSScriptRoot
$uproject = Join-Path $proj "Supercut.uproject"
$logDir = Join-Path $proj "Saved\Logs"
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force $logDir | Out-Null
$log = Join-Path $logDir "ubt_$Target.log"
$pchDir = Join-Path $proj "Intermediate\Build\Win64\x64\$Target\Development"

for ($try = 1; $try -le 4; $try++) {
    & "$Engine\Engine\Build\BatchFiles\Build.bat" $Target Win64 Development "-project=$uproject" -waitmutex "-MaxParallelActions=$Jobs" "-Log=$log" | Out-Null
    $code = $LASTEXITCODE
    if ($code -eq 0) { Write-Output "build $Target on ${Engine}: exit 0 (try $try)"; exit 0 }
    $badHeader = Select-String -Path $log -Pattern "msc1\.cpp', line 1589" -Quiet
    if (-not $badHeader -or $try -eq 4) {
        Select-String -Path $log -Pattern "error |Result:" | Select-Object -First 20 | ForEach-Object { $_.Line }
        Write-Output "build $Target on ${Engine}: exit $code (try $try). Log: $log"
        exit $code
    }

 "content": "# Orthographic point views of a prop in Unreal axes (x = bx, y = -by, z = bz from the FBX vertices), coloured from its\n# texture: top (x right, +y down, like roommap.py), front (x right, z up) and side (y right, z up). Finds which way a\n# film light, camera or chair faces. Usage: python -I gear_views.py <fbx> <png> <out.png>\nimport os\nimport sys\n\nimport numpy as np\nfrom PIL import Image, ImageDraw\n\nsys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))\nimport fbxread\n\nm = fbxread.mesh(sys.argv[1])\ntex = np.asarray(Image.open(sys.argv[2]).convert(\"RGB\"))\nH, W, _ = tex.shape\nidx = np.where(m[\"pvi\"] < 0, ~m[\"pvi\"], m[\"pvi\"])\nP = m[\"verts\"][idx] * np.array([1, -1, 1])\nUV = m[\"uv\"][m[\"uvi\"]]\nC = tex[np.clip((1 - UV[:, 1] % 1) * H, 0, H - 1).astype(int), np.clip((UV[:, 0] % 1) * W, 0, W - 1).astype(int)]\nspan = (P.max(0) - P.min(0)).max() * 1.1\nS = 300 / span\nimg = Image.new(\"RGB\", (960, 330), (255, 255, 255))\nd = ImageDraw.Draw(img)\nmid = (P.max(0) + P.min(0)) / 2\nfor k, (a, b, flip) in enumerate(((0, 1, 1), (0, 2, -1), (1, 2, -1))):\n    ox, oy = k * 320 + 160, 165\n    order = np.argsort(P[:, 3 - a - b] * (1 if k else 1))\n    for p, c in zip(P[order], C[order]):\n        x, y = ox + (p[a] - mid[a]) * S, oy + flip * (p[b] - mid[b]) * S\n        d.point((x, y), fill=tuple(int(v) for v in c))\n    d.text((k * 320 + 5, 5), [\"top: x right, +y down\", \"front: x right, z up\", \"side: y right, z up\"][k], fill=(0, 0, 0))\nimg.save(sys.argv[3])\nprint(os.path.basename(sys.argv[1]), \"min\", np.round(P.min(0), 1), \"max\", np.round(P.max(0), 1))\n"
}

room, short name, (view A yaw, pitch), (view B yaw, pitch)\n    \"fight/01_wind_machine\": (\"01\", (-82, 12), (100, 12)),\n    \"puzzle/a_the_cue\": (\"a\", (55, 10), (-100, 35)),\n    \"fight/02_stunt_run\": (\"02\", (-35, 8), (0, 0)),\n    \"fight/03_long_lens\": (\"03\", (55, 0), (-10, 15)),\n    \"puzzle/b_the_wild_wall\": (\"b\", (40, 15), (130, 30)),\n    \"fight/04_hot_set\": (\"04\", (-55, 10), (15, 10)),\n    \"puzzle/c_the_cutaway\": (\"c\", (-60, 5), (57, 25)),\n    \"fight/05_martini_shot\": (\"05\", (80, 0), (-10, 15)),\n}\n\n\ndef views(t, short, a, b, state):\n    lamp = LAMP[short]\n    return [\n        \"%.2f look %d %d\" % (t, a[0], a[1]), \"%.2f shot %s_A_%s\" % (t + 0.25, short, state),\n        \"%.2f look %d %d\" % (t + 0.4, b[0], b[1]), \"%.2f shot %s_B_%s\" % (t + 0.65, short, state),\n        \"%.2f lookat %.0f %.0f %.0f\" % (t + 0.8, *lamp), \"%.2f shot %s_L_%s\" % (t + 1.05, short, state),\n    ]\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    out = sys.argv[1]\n    os.makedirs(out, exist_ok=True)\n    for room, (short, a, b) in ROOMS.items():\n        if short == \"01\":\n            # # Contact sheet: the given pictures two to a row at 480 wide, with their names. Usage: sheet.py <out> <png>...
import os, sys
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw
files = sys.argv[2:]
W, H = 480, 270
sheet = Image.new("RGB", (2 * W, H * ((len(files) + 1) // 2)), (0, 0, 0))
d = ImageDraw.Draw(sheet)
for n, f in enumerate(files):
    im = Image.open(f).convert("RGB").resize((W, H))
    sheet.paste(im, ((n % 2) * W, (n // 2) * H))
    d.text(((n % 2) * W + 5, (n // 2) * H + 5), os.path.basename(f), fill=(255, 255, 0))
sheet.save(sys.argv[1])
EOF

- **The Bash tool: a backslash right before `$` in a double-quoted Windows path keeps the `$` literal** (14 Nov 2026,
  verified). `"-abslog=$O\logs\$name.log"` wrote a file named `logs$name.log`; `"$O\stream\$mode"` did the same.
  Build each Windows file path with `cygpath -aw "$dir/$name.log"`. In Python heredocs `'\'` also arrived as `'\'`:
  use `os.sep` or `chr(92)`.
- **The engine's HIGH level renders at 87 percent resolution scale** (14 Nov 2026, verified on pc2). The saved file after the
  first start's HIGH has `sg.ResolutionQuality=87`; EPIC has 100, LOW 50 (lane perf2). It did not change the hatching.
- **`USubmixEffectDynamicsProcessorPreset::SetSettings` changes a running limiter at once** (14 Nov 2026, verified in a
  recorded F5 run). It calls `UpdateSettings`, which copies to `SettingsCopy` and every running effect's `OnPresetChanged`
  reads `InputGainDb` from it. Outside an editor script the preset's `Settings` UPROPERTY is not rewritten
  (`ShouldUpdateSavedSettings` is false in a game), so read the live value with `GetSettings()`.

cd "[notes]/unreal"; file GOTCHAS.md; cat >> GOTCHAS.md <<'EOF'

## SUPERCUT props1 lane: set props (14 Nov 2026, c4, engine 5.9 preview)

- **`StaticMeshEditorSubsystem` has no instance under `-run=pythonscript`** (14 Nov 2026, verified).
  `unreal.get_editor_subsystem(unreal.StaticMeshEditorSubsystem)` returned None in the commandlet, so
  `add_simple_collisions` failed with "NoneType has no attribute". `Tools/make_props.py` imports with no collision and
  the game gives film gear a `UBoxComponent` sized from `UStaticMesh::GetBoundingBox()` (`SupercutShapes::AddSetProp`).
- **A failed import run leaves assets that break the next run** (14 Nov 2026, verified). After a run that died half way,
  `EditorAssetLibrary.delete_directory("/Game/Props/Set")` returned False (one texture stayed on disk) and the new
  M_SetProp found a NULL texture. Delete the folder on disk (only when every file in it is yours) and run again.
- **These Blender FBX files come into Unreal with y flipped** (14 Nov 2026, verified with the lamp). The vertices are
  stored Blender Z up with Lcl Rotation -90 on X; with Convert Scene on, Unreal (x, y, z) = Blender (x, -y, z).
  A point measured in Blender needs its y negated before it is used in C++.
- **`AActor::GetComponentsBoundingBox()` counts only parts that collide** (14 Nov 2026, verified against
  `ASupercutRoom::BuildLight`). Anything added to a room before `BuildLight` with collision moves the lamp. Set props
  are queued and built after the light; a desk thing has no collision and gear boxes come after the light too.
- **Desk-size props on the desk cannot be seen from inside a room** (14 Nov 2026, verified in pictures). Walls are
  480 to 650 cm, the eye is about 160 cm up and the tallest desk thing (glue, 375 cm) stands on the desk at -50 cm.
  To be seen, a desk thing leans on a wall's top edge (ruler, set square) or lies across a wall top (pencil, knife).
- **The soundstage fixture lists every built part** (14 Nov 2026, verified). Adding a part to every room (here the lamp
  mesh and its bulb) fails `SoundstageFileBuildsTheSamePiecesAsTheOldCode` until the new lines are added to
  `Source/Supercut/SupercutTestRoomPieces.txt` (sorted, CRLF) and the count in the test is raised. A spot light is a
  `UPointLightComponent`, so its "lamp at" line in the fixture proves the light did not move.
EOF

cd "[notes]/unreal/megajam-2026/lanes/props1/tools"; cat >> bulb_radius.py <<'EOF'
# The points within 130 cm: their middle and a sphere fitted to them (least squares).
p = v[d < 130]
A = np.c_[2 * p, np.ones(len(p))]
sol = np.linalg.lstsq(A, (p ** 2).sum(1), rcond=None)[0]
centre = sol[:3]
print("near points", len(p), "middle", np.round(p.mean(0), 1), "fitted centre", np.round(centre, 1),
      "radius", round(float(np.sqrt(sol[3] + centre @ centre)), 1))
q = np.linalg.norm(p - centre, axis=1)
print("distance from fitted centre: min %.1f, median %.1f, max %.1f" % (q.min(), np.median(q), q.max()))
EOF

// The lamp itself (SM_Lamp), standing on the desk with its bulb at the light. Its own bulb is the middle of the
	// shade's ball, measured in Blender: BulbInMesh in the mesh's own space, with the shade's mouth facing yaw 120 and
	// 60 degrees down. Only its yaw is turned, so the base stays flat on the desk and the shade points 10 degrees lower
	// than the light. One uniform scale puts the bulb at the light's height. The lamp throws no shadow: its shade is
	// round the light and would block it.
	const FVector BulbInMesh(1.5, 244.7, 866.7);
	const float ShadeYawInMesh = 120.f;
	const float BulbRadiusInMesh = 110.f;   // the mesh's own grey bulb reaches 56 to 128 cm from BulbInMesh
	const float LampScale = (LampAt.Z - Model.Min.Z) / BulbInMesh.Z;
	const FRotator LampTurn(0.f, (-ToLamp).Rotation().Yaw - ShadeYawInMesh, 0.f);
	const FVector LampBase = LampAt - LampTurn.RotateVector(BulbInMesh * LampScale);
	const SupercutShapes::FSetProp* LampProp = SupercutShapes::FindSetProp(TEXT("lamp"));
	checkf(LampProp, TEXT("The set prop list has no lamp"));
	UStaticMeshComponent* LampMesh = SupercutShapes::AddSetProp(this, RootComponent, *LampProp, LampBase, LampTurn, LampScale);
	LampMesh->SetCastShadow(false);
	// The bulb: a glowing ball in the lamp's colour over the mesh's own grey bulb, inside the shade. A Glow part keeps
	// its live colour in frozen time (ESketch::Signal).
	UStaticMeshComponent* Bulb = AddShape(ESupercutShape::Sphere, LampAt, FRotator::ZeroRotator, FVector(BulbRadiusInMesh * 2.f * LampScale),
		SupercutShapes::Glow(this, FLinearColor::MakeFromColorTemperature(Tuning.LampKelvin), 3.f), false);
	Bulb->SetCastShadow(false);
	UE_LOG(LogSupercut, Display, TEXT("LIGHT lamp mesh base at %s, scale %.2f, yaw %.0f"), *LampBase.ToCompactString(), LampScale, LampTurn.Yaw);
}

 "content": "# props1 HANDOFF: set props in SUPERCUT\n\nLane props1, 14 Nov 2026, c4, UE 5.9, repo `D:\\UE\\Projects\\Supercut59`, branch `ue59`. Not pushed.\n\n## What was built\n\n- **13 set props imported.** `Art/props_gen` holds the FBX and base colour PNG of each (SOURCE.md names lanes rodin1,\n  rodin2 and rodin3). `Tools/make_props.py` imports them all into `Content/Props/Set`: 13 static meshes, 13 textures\n  (sRGB, default compression, World group), one material `M_SetProp` (ColorTex into Base Colour, Rough 0.8) and one\n  instance per prop. No Nanite, no lightmap UVs, no collision in the asset. Triangles: 2,998 or 3,000 each, the lamp\n  8,000. `Tools/make_figures.py` used to clear all of `/Game/Props`; it now clears only what it makes there.\n- **The lamp in every room.** `ASupercutRoom::BuildLight` stands `SM_Lamp` on the desk (the model's lowest point) with\n  its bulb at the desk light. Only its yaw turns (base flat on the desk), and one uniform scale (2.28 to 3.26 in the\n  eight rooms) puts the bulb at the light's height. The lamp throws no shadow, so its shade cannot block the light.\n  A glowing ball (M_Glow, the lamp's colour temperature, strength 3) sits over the mesh's own grey bulb. The light\n  (position, rotation, candelas, cone, colour, softness) is not touched: the `LIGHT lamp at` lines of all 8 rooms are\n  the same as before, and the soundstage fixture's light line is unchanged.\n- **The `dress` line.** `dress name=<set prop> at=x,y,z turn=pitch,yaw,roll [scale=1]` places a set prop with the\n  centre of its base at `at`. It is read like every other piece. An unknown name (the error lists the 12 names), the\n  lamp, or a scale of 0 or less is refused with the file and line; a missing mesh stops the game with a fatal error\n  that names the asset and the import script. Dress props are queued and built after the light, so they never move it.\n- **Two kinds.** Desk things (ruler, pencil, glue, tape, set_square, knife) collide with nothing. # Contact sheet: the given pictures two to a row at 480 wide, with their names. Usage: sheet.py <out> <png>...
import os, sys
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw
files = sys.argv[2:]
W, H = 480, 270
sheet = Image.new("RGB", (2 * W, H * ((len(files) + 1) // 2)), (0, 0, 0))
d = ImageDraw.Draw(sheet)
for n, f in enumerate(files):
    im = Image.open(f).convert("RGB").resize((W, H))
    sheet.paste(im, ((n % 2) * W, (n // 2) * H))
    d.text(((n % 2) * W + 5, (n // 2) * H + 5), os.path.basename(f), fill=(255, 255, 0))
sheet.save(sys.argv[1])
```

# Build farm for SUPERCUT

Lane farm1, 14 Nov 2026. Other PCs build, test, package and run SUPERCUT for lanes on c4. Git, agents and the
source of truth stay on c4. A farm PC holds a plain copy of a project folder (a "mirror"), never a git repo.
Nothing is ever pushed with git.

## Which PCs are ready

| PC | Root | Ready | Build | Tests | Package | Scripted run | Lanes at once |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `[pc-b]` | `C:\UE` | **yes** (17:33) | yes | yes | Development and Shipping | yes, offscreen | 2 (builds queue, see below) |
| `pc2` | `C:\UE` | **yes** (18:02) | yes | yes | Development | yes, offscreen, slow: add `-TimeoutSeconds 900` | 1 (16 GB RAM, Studio windows open) |
| `[pc-c]` | `F:\UE` | **yes** (17:58) | yes | yes | Development | yes, offscreen | 2 (builds queue, see below) |
| `pc4` | `C:\UE` | **compile only** (18:09) | yes (editor and game targets) | **no** | **no** | **no** | 1 (12 GB RAM, runs hot) |

pc4: Smart App Control (Windows code integrity policy `VerifiedAndReputableDesktop`, enforced) blocks every DLL we
compile. The editor could not load `UnrealEditor-Supercut.dll` (`GetLastError=4551`, Code Integrity event 3077), so
tests, cooking and the game cannot run there. Builds do run: use pc4 only to check that a change compiles
(`build pc4 <name> <logs> -Jobs 4`, and `-Target Supercut -Jobs 4` for the game target). Nothing on its policy was
changed and nothing should be; turning Smart App Control off is the owner's call.

The root table also sits at the top of `farm/farm.sh` (`root_of`). On every PC: engine in `<root>\UE_5.9`, mirrors in
`<root>\Farm\<name>`, packages in `<root>\Farm\_builds\<name>`, step logs in `<root>\Farm\_out\<name>\<step>`, farm
scripts in `<root>\Farm\_farm`.

# props1 HANDOFF: set props in SUPERCUT

Lane props1, 14 Nov 2026, c4, UE 5.9, repo `D:\UE\Projects\Supercut59`, branch `ue59`. Not pushed.

## What was built

- **13 set props imported.** `Art/props_gen` holds the FBX and base colour PNG of each (SOURCE.md names lanes rodin1,
  rodin2 and rodin3). `Tools/make_props.py` imports them all into `Content/Props/Set`: 13 static meshes, 13 textures
  (sRGB, default compression, World group), one material `M_SetProp` (ColorTex into Base Colour, Rough 0.8) and one
  instance per prop. No Nanite, no lightmap UVs, no collision in the asset. Triangles: 2,998 or 3,000 each, the lamp
  8,000. `Tools/make_figures.py` used to clear all of `/Game/Props`; it now clears only what it makes there.
- **The lamp in every room.** `ASupercutRoom::BuildLight` stands `SM_Lamp` on the desk (the model's lowest point) with
  its bulb at the desk light. Only its yaw turns (base flat on the desk), and one uniform scale (2.28 to 3.26 in the
  eight rooms) puts the bulb at the light's height. The lamp throws no shadow, so its shade cannot block the light.
  A glowing ball (M_Glow, the lamp's colour temperature, strength 3) sits over the mesh's own grey bulb. The light
  (position, rotation, candelas, cone, colour, softness) is not touched: the `LIGHT lamp at` lines of all 8 rooms are
  the same as before, and the soundstage fixture's light line is unchanged.
- **The `dress` line.** `dress name=<set prop> at=x,y,z turn=pitch,yaw,roll [scale=1]` places a set prop with the
  centre of its base at `at`. It is read like every other piece. An unknown name (the error lists the 13 names), the
  lamp, or a scale of 0 or less is refused with the file and line; a missing mesh stops the game with a fatal error
  that names the asset and the import script. Dress props are queued and built after the light, so they never move it.
- **Two kinds.** Desk things (ruler, pencil, glue, tape, set_square, knife) collide with nothing. Film gear (chair,

# SUPERCUT realistic props: shared spec for the prop lanes (14 Nov 2026)

## What the owner wants (play-test notes, 14 Nov, ~17:40 SGT)

> "environment is too bare. we have so much 3d generation credits, ... make more props. also the chair fails.

> green screens, fill lamps, boom mics, cameras, and so much more"

The look is now REALISTIC: a working film soundstage at real-world scale. The 13 Nov "maquette" card-and-balsa
look in GAME.md and rodin2's "muted, pale balsa" prompt block NO LONGER APPLY to props. Real scale (cm, 1:1), not
the x25 set scale.

## Sources, in this order

1. Free CC0 models and textures that need no login: Poly Haven (models, textures, HDRIs), ambientCG (textures).
   Record each in a `SOURCE.txt` (page, download date, licence words, file hashes), like
   `lanes/arms1/downloads/*/SOURCE.txt`. These are sourced assets: the jam thread adds them to SUBMISSION.md.

   drops files on disk, they get used.

   an earlier output) -> Hyper3D Rodin via `tools/rodin/rodin.py` with a ledger in your lane folder -> Blender clean-up.
   Picture style: product photo of the real object, neutral grey studio background, three-quarter view, worn and used,
   real materials (powder-coated steel, aluminium, rubber, canvas, plywood, gaffer tape). Rodin: try
   `Gen-2.5-High` with `--set texture_mode=extreme-high` (2.5 credits) on the first prop of a kind; drop to cheaper
   settings only if the result is just as good. Never re-submit a paid task. Hyper3D credits end 20 Nov 23:59 SGT.
4. Built in Blender by script, for clean hard-surface and modular parts (stands, truss, scaffolding, track), with CC0
   PBR textures.

## Hard rules

- SUPERCUT only. Generated fresh for this game; nothing shared with other games' batches either way.

# Imports the set props: the desk lamp, the giant desk things and the model film gear (Art/props_gen, see SOURCE.md there).
# Every Art/props_gen/SM_<Name>.fbx comes in as /Game/Props/Set/SM_<Name>, with its T_<Name>_BC.png as
# /Game/Props/Set/Textures/T_<Name>_BC and one material instance MI_<Name> of M_SetProp. Which name is a desk thing and
# which is film gear, and where they stand, is the game's business (SupercutShapes::SetProps and the dress lines of
# room files), so a new prop here needs no list entry.
#

#   D:\UE\UE_5.9\Engine\Binaries\Win64\UnrealEditor-Cmd.exe D:\UE\Projects\Supercut59\Supercut.uproject
#     -run=pythonscript -Script=D:\UE\Projects\Supercut59\Tools\make_props.py -AllowCommandletRendering -unattended -nopause -nosplash
#
# Safe to run again: it deletes and remakes everything under /Game/Props/Set, and nothing else.
# Tools/make_held.py imports the held items with the same functions.
# Every FBX goes through the legacy FBX importer, as in make_figures.py: an import task with an explicit FbxFactory skips
# Interchange and takes its options from the task's FbxImportUI.

def clear(folder):
    if EAL.does_directory_exist(folder) and not EAL.delete_directory(folder):
        raise RuntimeError("could not delete " + folder)


def fresh(name, folder, asset_class, factory):
    asset = TOOLS.create_asset(name, folder, asset_class, factory)
    if asset is None:
        raise RuntimeError("could not create " + folder + "/" + name)
    return asset


def import_texture(source, folder, name):
    # A base colour map: sRGB, default (BC1) compression, mips, streamed like any texture a mesh shows.
    if not os.path.isfile(source):

    task = unreal.AssetImportTask()
    task.set_editor_property("filename", source)

namespace
{
	template <typename T>
	T* LoadOrDie(const TCHAR* Path)
	{
		T* Object = LoadObject<T>(nullptr, Path);
		if (!Object)
		{
			UE_LOG(LogSupercut, Fatal, TEXT("Missing asset %s. Meshes come from the engine's BasicShapes folder; materials are made by Tools/make_assets.py."), Path);
		}
		return Object;
	}
}

UStaticMesh* SupercutShapes::Mesh(ESupercutShape Shape)
{
	switch (Shape)
	{
	case ESupercutShape::Cube:     return LoadOrDie<UStaticMesh>(TEXT("/Engine/BasicShapes/Cube.Cube"));
	case ESupercutShape::Sphere:   return LoadOrDie<UStaticMesh>(TEXT("/Engine/BasicShapes/Sphere.Sphere"));
	case ESupercutShape::Cylinder: return LoadOrDie<UStaticMesh>(TEXT("/Engine/BasicShapes/Cylinder.Cylinder"));
	case ESupercutShape::Cone:     return LoadOrDie<UStaticMesh>(TEXT("/Engine/BasicShapes/Cone.Cone"));
	}
	checkNoEntry();
	return nullptr;
}

UMaterialInstanceDynamic* SupercutShapes::Solid(UObject* Outer, const FLinearColor& Color, float Roughness, const FLinearColor& Glow)
{
	UMaterialInterface* Base = LoadOrDie<UMaterialInterface>(TEXT("/Game/Materials/M_Solid.M_Solid"));
	UMaterialInstanceDynamic* Material = UMaterialInstanceDynamic::Create(Base, Outer);
	Material->SetVectorParameterValue(TEXT("Color"), Color);
	Material->SetScalarParameterValue(TEXT("Rough"), Roughness);
	Material->SetVectorParameterValue(TEXT("Glow"), Glow);
	return Material;
}

UMaterialInterface* SupercutShapes::Maquette(const TCHAR* Name)
{
	return LoadOrDie<UMaterialInterface>(*FString::Printf(TEXT("/Game/Materials/Maquette/%s.%s"), Name, Name));
}

void SupercutShapes::MarkForSketch(UPrimitiveComponent* Part, ESketch Kind)
{
	Part->SetRenderCustomDepth(true);
	Part->SetCustomDepthStencilValue(static_cast<int32>(Kind));
}

// The piece types a room file can use, apart from the ones that live with their own actor
// (the film can registers itself in SupercutFilmCan.cpp, and a new piece type should do the same).

// Each block below is one piece type: the word that starts its line, how many a room may hold, and

#include "SupercutGrunt.h"

namespace
{
	/** Reads from= and to= as the two opposite corners of a box. from must be the lower corner on every axis. */
	FBox Corners(FSupercutPieceReader& In)
	{
		const FVector From = In.Vector(TEXT("from"));
		const FVector To = In.Vector(TEXT("to"));
		if (From.X >= To.X || From.Y >= To.Y || From.Z >= To.Z)
		{
			In.Fail(FString::Printf(TEXT("from=%.0f,%.0f,%.0f must be lower than to=%.0f,%.0f,%.0f on x, y and z"), From.X, From.Y, From.Z, To.X, To.Y, To.Z));
		}
		return FBox(From, To);
	}

	FString Role(FSupercutPieceReader& In)
	{
		const FString Word = In.Word(TEXT("role"));
		if (!Word.IsEmpty() && !ASupercutRoom::IsRole(Word))
		{
			In.Fail(FString::Printf(TEXT("role=%s is not a colour role. The roles are: %s"), *Word, *ASupercutRoom::RoleNames()));
		}
		return Word;
	}

		bool bAccent;   // a coloured lamp that marks a place, not one that lights the room

	};
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- For piece types

bool ASupercutRoom::IsRole(const FString& RoleName)
{
	return FindRole(RoleName) != nullptr;
}

FString ASupercutRoom::RoleNames()
{
	TArray<FString> Names;
	for (const FSurfaceRole& Role : Roles)
	{
		Names.Add(Role.Name);
	}
	return FString::Join(Names, TEXT(", "));
}

UMaterialInterface* ASupercutRoom::RoleMaterial(const FString& RoleName)
{
	if (const TObjectPtr<UMaterialInterface>* Made = RoleMaterials.Find(RoleName))
	{
		return *Made;
	}
	const FSurfaceRole* Found = FindRole(RoleName);
	checkf(Found, TEXT("Room %s: \"%s\" is not a colour role. A piece type must check the word with ASupercutRoom::IsRole when it reads its line."), *RoomName, *RoleName);
	UMaterialInterface* Material = Found->Maquette ? SupercutShapes::Maquette(Found->Maquette)
		: Found->bGlows ? SupercutShapes::Glow(this, SupercutShapes::SignalColor(Found->Signal), SignalGlow(Found->Signal))
		: SupercutShapes::Solid(this, Found->Color, Found->Rough, Found->Strength > 0.f ? Found->Color * Found->Strength : FLinearColor::Black);
	if (RoleName == TEXT("floor"))
	{
		// The cutting mat takes a shade of its own, so the lamp can stay right for the foam walls.
		UMaterialInstanceDynamic* Mat = UMaterialInstanceDynamic::Create(Material, this);
		const float Shade = FSupercutTuning::Get().MatShade;
		Mat->SetVectorParameterValue(TEXT("Tint"), FLinearColor(Shade, Shade, Shade));
		Material = Mat;
	}
	RoleMaterials.Add(RoleName, Material);
	return Material;
}

UStaticMeshComponent* ASupercutRoom::AddShape(ESupercutShape Shape, const FVector& Location, const FRotator& Rotation, const FVector& SizeCm, UMaterialInterface* Material, bool bSolid)

void ASupercutShot::Impact(const FHitResult& Hit)
{
	AActor* Other = Hit.GetActor();
	UE_LOG(LogSupercut, Display, TEXT("SHOT lands: %s (%s) on %s after %.0f cm"), *GetName(), bFromPlayer ? TEXT("player") : TEXT("enemy"),
		Other ? *Other->GetName() : TEXT("nothing"), Travelled);
	if (bFromPlayer)
	{
		if (ASupercutEnemy* Enemy = Cast<ASupercutEnemy>(Other))
		{
			const bool bWasAlive = !Enemy->IsDying();
			Enemy->TakeHit(SupercutUpgrades::HitDamage(*this, FSupercutTuning::Get().RevolverDamage), Velocity.GetSafeNormal());
			const bool bKill = bWasAlive && Enemy->IsDying();
			if (bKill)
			{
				USupercutRun::Get(this).NoteKill(*this);
			}
			if (bWasAlive)
			{
				CastChecked<ASupercutCharacter>(Shooter.Get())->NoteHitLanded(bKill);
				const FSupercutTuning& Tuning = FSupercutTuning::Get();
				ASupercutChips::Throw(GetWorld(), Hit.ImpactPoint, Velocity, bKill ? Tuning.KillChipCount : Tuning.HitChipCount);
			}
			if (SupercutUpgrades::PassesThrough(*this))
			{
				// Not spent: it flies on from here and will not hit this enemy again.
				PassedThrough.Add(Enemy);
				UE_LOG(LogSupercut, Display, TEXT("SHOT passes through: %s flies on"), *GetName());
				return;
			}
		}
		else if (ASupercutPlates* Plates = Cast<ASupercutPlates>(Other))
		{
			Plates->TakeShot(Hit.GetComponent(), FireNumber, HungInFreeze);
		}
		else if (ASupercutSwitch* Switch = Cast<ASupercutSwitch>(Other))
		{
			Switch->TakeShot();
		}
		else if (!Cast<ASupercutCharacter>(Other))
		{
			USupercutAudio::Get(this).PlayAt(TEXT("shot_hit_wall"), Hit.ImpactPoint);
			// A mark stays only on a drawn part that never moves: not on a machine or a door, not on a gear piece's box.
			const UPrimitiveComponent* Surface = Hit.GetComponent();
			if (Surface && Surface->Mobility == EComponentMobility::Static && Surface->IsA<UStaticMeshComponent>())
			{
				ASupercutRoom* Room = USupercutRun::Get(this).GetRoom();
				checkf(Room, TEXT("%s hit %s with no room in play"), *GetName(), *GetNameSafe(Other));
				Room->GetLitter().AddWallMark(Hit.ImpactPoint, Hit.ImpactNormal);
			}
		}
	}
	else if (ASupercutCharacter* Player = Cast<ASupercutCharacter>(Other))
	{
		Player->TakeHit(PlayerDamage, Origin, PlayerHitCause);
	}

	bSpent = true;
	SpentAge = 0.f;
	Tail->SetVisibility(false);
	USupercutAudio::Get(this).Stop(Hum);
	Hum = nullptr;
}

// SUPERCUT frozen-time sketch. Body of ONE Material Custom node (Output Type: CMOT Float 3), wired to
// Emissive Color of a material with Material Domain = Post Process.
// A port of shade() in the sketchfx lane's sketchfx.py. Tools/make_assets.py reads this file into M_SketchFreeze.

//
// ---- Custom node input pins (name -> what to wire) ----
//   PaperTex     TextureObject  T_Sketch_Paper   (the node then also gives PaperTexSampler)
//   HatchTex     TextureObject  T_Sketch_Hatch   (HatchTexSampler)
//   Blend        ScalarParameter "Blend", 0 live .. 1 frozen
//   ToneLo       ScalarParameter "ToneLo": how bright the lit picture must be to stay bare paper is 1 - ToneLo.

//   StudioTone   ScalarParameter "StudioTone": the fixed pencil tone of the studio round the model, 0 paper .. 1 darkest

def make_sketch_collection():
    # Values every material can read, set by the player each frame: Blend (0 live .. 1 frozen, the same as the
    # sketch's) and FrozenGlow (the strength glows fall to when frozen, FSupercutTuning::SketchFrozenGlow).
    collection = fresh("MPC_Sketch", "/Game/Materials", unreal.MaterialParameterCollection,
                       unreal.MaterialParameterCollectionFactoryNew())
    scalars = []
    for name, default in (("Blend", 0.0), ("FrozenGlow", 1.0)):
        scalar = unreal.CollectionScalarParameter()    # its constructor gives it a new Id
        scalar.set_editor_property("parameter_name", name)
        scalar.set_editor_property("default_value", default)
        scalars.append(scalar)
    collection.set_editor_property("scalar_parameters", scalars)
    if not EAL.save_loaded_asset(collection):
        raise RuntimeError("MPC_Sketch not saved")
    return collection

## Materials built by script (both engines)

- **A material that fails to compile still returns success from every call.** Only the log says so, as
  a Warning, not an Error: "LogMaterial: Warning: ... Failed to compile Material for platform PCD3D_SM6,

  building any material. (13 Nov 2026, verified in 5.9, lane probe59)
- **A new ComponentMask has R and G on.** Feeding it into a float3 gives "Arithmetic between types
  float3 and float2". Set the channels you want explicitly. (13 Nov 2026, verified in 5.9)
- **A game window started from an agent shell stays open.** Start the packaged exe with
  `Start-Process -PassThru`, wait for the log line you need, then stop the process by id.

## SUPERCUT props1 lane: set props (14 Nov 2026, c4, engine 5.9 preview)

  the game gives film gear a `UBoxComponent` sized from `UStaticMesh::GetBoundingBox()` (`SupercutShapes::AddSetProp`).

  M_SetProp found a NULL texture. Delete the folder on disk (only when every file in it is yours) and run again.
- **These Blender FBX files come into Unreal with y flipped** (14 Nov 2026, verified with the lamp). The vertices are
  stored Blender Z up with Lcl Rotation -90 on X; with Convert Scene on, Unreal (x, y, z) = Blender (x, -y, z).
  A point measured in Blender needs its y negated before it is used in C++.
- **`AActor::GetComponentsBoundingBox()` counts only parts that collide** (14 Nov 2026, verified against

  are queued and built after the light; a desk thing has no collision and gear boxes come after the light too.

struct FSupercutRoomNote
{

	int32 Number = 0;

};

mkdir -p "[notes]/unreal/megajam-2026/lanes/props1/tools2"; cat > "[notes]/unreal/megajam-2026/lanes/props1/tools2/tex_sheet.py" <<'EOF'
# Contact sheet of every T_*_BC.png in a batch folder, plus a hue census for the game's signal colours.
# Usage: python -I tex_sheet.py <batch folder> <out.jpg>
import colorsys, glob, os, sys
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw
src, out = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
files = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(src, "T_*_BC.png")))
cell = 320
sheet = Image.new("RGB", (cell * 4, (cell + 20) * ((len(files) + 3) // 4)), (40, 40, 40))
d = ImageDraw.Draw(sheet)
for i, f in enumerate(files):
    im = Image.open(f).convert("RGB")
    small = im.resize((cell, cell))
    x, y = (i % 4) * cell, (i // 4) * (cell + 20)
    sheet.paste(small, (x, y + 20))
    d.text((x + 4, y + 4), os.path.basename(f), fill=(255, 255, 255))
    px = im.resize((256, 256)).getdata()
    sig = {"yellow": 0, "red-orange": 0, "green": 0, "cyan": 0}
    for r, g, b in px:
        h, s, v = colorsys.rgb_to_hsv(r / 255, g / 255, b / 255)
        if s < 0.35 or v < 0.25:
            continue
        deg = h * 360
        if 40 <= deg < 70: sig["yellow"] += 1
        elif deg < 40 or deg >= 345: sig["red-orange"] += 1
        elif 80 <= deg < 160: sig["green"] += 1
        elif 160 <= deg < 200: sig["cyan"] += 1
    n = len(px)
    print(os.path.basename(f), " ".join("%s %.1f%%" % (k, 100 * v / n) for k, v in sig.items()))
sheet.save(out, quality=85)
EOF

pull() {
  local host=$1 src=$2 dst=$3 un cn
  mkdir -p "$dst"
  scp -r -q "$host:$src" "$dst/" || return 1
  un=$(ssh "$host" 'echo %USERNAME%' | tr -d '\r\n'); cn=$(ssh "$host" 'echo %COMPUTERNAME%' | tr -d '\r\n')
  find "$dst" -type f \( -name '*.log' -o -name '*.txt' -o -name '*.ini' -o -name '*.csv' \) -print0 |
    xargs -0 -r sed -i -e "s#$un#USER#Ig" -e "s#$cn#PC#Ig"
}

step() {   # step <name of step> <host> <name> <log folder> [args...]
  local s=$1 host=$2 name=$3 logs=$4; shift 4
  local root; root=$(root_of "$host") || exit $?
  local af=''
  if [ $# -gt 0 ]; then
    af="$root\\Farm\\_out\\$name.$s.args.txt"
    local tmp; tmp=$(mktemp)
    printf '%s\r\n' "$@" > "$tmp"
    ssh "$host" "if not exist $root\\Farm\\_out mkdir $root\\Farm\\_out" && scp -q "$tmp" "$host:$(fwd "$af")" || exit 1
    rm -f "$tmp"
  fi
  ssh "$host" "powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $root\\Farm\\_farm\\step.ps1 -Root $root -Name $name -Step $s ${af:+-ArgsFile $af}"
  local code=$?
  rm -rf "${logs:?}/$s"
  pull "$host" "$(fwd "$root")/Farm/_out/$name/$s" "$logs" || echo "FARM could not fetch the logs of $s" >&2
  exit $code
}
```

### Sat 14 Nov 18:28:03 · Brief from the orchestrating agent

GLASSBOX-MEGAJAM-2026 lane=props1 (from the jam thread: the hall kit's first batch is here, and it differs from the props)

`unreal\megajam-2026\lanes\hall1\out\batch1\` holds 19 hall pieces (`SM_Hall_<Name>.fbx` + `.json`, verified by that lane: `out\verify.json`, 19 of 19). **Import them right after your step 2 (the catalogue), as its own commit, before the blocking work**, because a second lane that builds the hall around each room starts from your branch as soon as that commit exists. Write the commit's hash and time into your LOG.md when it is done.

How the hall kit differs from the props:

1. **Shared textures, not one set per piece.** One copy in `lanes\hall1\out\textures\` (five sets, each BC, N in DirectX, ORM, 2048, with a SOURCE.txt). Five materials by slot name: `M_Hall_Concrete`, `M_Hall_Wall`, `M_Hall_Padding`, `M_Hall_Roof`, `M_Hall_Kit`. Each piece's JSON lists its `materials` and `textures`. Make the five material instances once and assign them by the mesh's slot names. The first four tile (wrap addressing); `M_Hall_Kit` is an atlas and may clamp. A piece has one or two slots. Copy the textures folder into your `Art\props_real\hall1\textures\` beside the batch.
2. Hall textures are seen from far away over the room's walls, except the floor. Keep the concrete at 2048 and import the others at 1024 unless a picture shows that is not enough.
3. The pieces were mirrored in Blender so that the usual import (Convert Scene on) lands every point of the JSONs in Unreal axes. Check one asymmetric piece after import (a wall column or the scaffold ladder) against its JSON and say what you saw.
4. Lamp lens faces are pale, not emissive. The light JSONs carry `lens_at` and `beam_tilt_deg`; keep those fields in the catalogue line for lights (add `lens=x,y,z tilt=deg` to the line), the hall lane will use them.
5. The truss JSONs carry snap points `light_left_n` / `light_right_n`; pieces sit on a 400 cm grid (scaffold and truss also 200). You do not place the hall: import, catalogue with `category=hall_piece`, and put the pieces in the show room in a row of their own.
6. Hall pieces marked as blocking are far outside the play space. Give them the same simple box as other blocking props; nothing more.

A second hall batch follows (stage door, more lights, catwalk, roof pieces, and a sample layout JSON). Take it in your step 7 as planned. Sourced textures (Poly Haven and ambientCG, CC0) go into your sourced-assets list from the SOURCE.txt.

1	# Imports the realistic props the prop lanes deliver, and writes the catalogue the game and the level generator read.
2	#
3	# Source: every Art/props_real/<lane>/<batch>/SM_<Name>.fbx with its SM_<Name>.json and three textures
4	# T_<Name>_BC.png (base colour), T_<Name>_N.png (DirectX normal) and T_<Name>_ORM.png (occlusion, roughness, metallic),
5	# in the delivery format of unreal/megajam-2026/lanes/PROPS_REALISTIC_SPEC.md.
6	# Made here, in /Game/Props/Real:
7	#   SM_<Name>                    the mesh, no collision (the game gives a blocking prop a box from its catalogue size)
8	#   Textures/T_<Set>_BC, _N, _ORM one texture set per prop, or one per shared set (same_textures_as)
9	#   Materials/M_PropReal         the one master material; Materials/MI_<Set> one instance per texture set
10	# Written: Content/Props/catalogue.txt, one line per prop that passed the checks below.
11	#
12	# Safe to run again: a prop whose mesh already exists is not imported again and nothing of it is changed; a new batch
13	# folder is picked up. The catalogue is written from scratch every time. To redo one prop, delete its SM_, its MI_ and
14	# its textures (if no other prop shares them) and run again.
15	#
16	# Why a new script and not make_props.py: make_props.py deletes and remakes all of /Game/Props/Set on every run and
17	# imports a base colour only. This one must never touch a finished prop. It reuses make_props.import_mesh, so both
18	# import meshes the same way (legacy FBX importer, cm, no Nanite, no lightmap UVs, no collision).
19	#
20	# Run headless from PowerShell (not Git Bash, see unreal/GOTCHAS.md), one editor at a time:

void ASupercutGameMode::InitGame(const FString& MapName, const FString& Options, FString& ErrorMessage)
{
	Super::InitGame(MapName, Options, ErrorMessage);

#if !UE_BUILD_SHIPPING
	// Before anything is built from the numbers. The time system read the defaults at world start; Begin sets its rules again.
	// A Shipping build plays the numbers it was built with: it never reads Tuning.txt.
	SupercutTuningFile::Load(SupercutTuningFile::FilePath());
#endif

	FString RunName = TEXT("main");
	FString RoomName;
	int32 Seed = int32(FPlatformTime::Cycles64() & 0x7fffffff);
	FString UpgradeText;
	// Read in every build, so a Shipping build can be checked with a script.
	FParse::Value(FCommandLine::Get(), TEXT("-SupercutRun="), RunName);
	FParse::Value(FCommandLine::Get(), TEXT("-SupercutRoom="), RoomName);
	FParse::Value(FCommandLine::Get(), TEXT("-SupercutSeed="), Seed);
	FParse::Value(FCommandLine::Get(), TEXT("-SupercutUpgrades="), UpgradeText, false);   // false: read past the commas (Parse.cpp)
	TArray<FString> UpgradeNames;
	UpgradeText.ParseIntoArray(UpgradeNames, TEXT(","));
	TArray<FName> Upgrades;
	for (const FString& Name : UpgradeNames)
	{
		Upgrades.Add(FName(*Name));
	}

	// The first room has to stand before the player logs in, which is earlier than StartPlay.
	const TArray<FString> Rooms = RoomName.IsEmpty() ? SupercutRoomFile::LoadRunOrDie(RunName) : TArray<FString>{ RoomName };
	USupercutRun::Get(this).SetStartUpgrades(Upgrades);
	USupercutRun::Get(this).Begin(Rooms, Seed, USupercutRun::StartsAtTitle(FCommandLine::Get()));
}

AActor* ASupercutGameMode::ChoosePlayerStart_Implementation(AController* Player)
{
	// The engine wants an actor to stand for the start. The player's real place comes from the room file's start line.
	return USupercutRun::Get(this).GetRoom();
}

    s = open(path, newline='').read()

UStaticMeshComponent* ASupercutEnemy::AddPistol(bool bLong)
{
	check(Figure);
	UStaticMeshComponent* Gun = NewObject<UStaticMeshComponent>(this);
	Gun->SetStaticMesh(SupercutFigure::Pistol(bLong));
	Gun->SetCollisionProfileName(TEXT("NoCollision"));
	Gun->SetGenerateOverlapEvents(false);
	Gun->SetCanEverAffectNavigation(false);
	Gun->SetupAttachment(Figure, SupercutFigure::HandBone);
	Gun->SetRelativeTransform(SupercutFigure::PistolOnHand());
	SupercutShapes::MarkForSketch(Gun, SupercutShapes::ESketch::Figure);
	Gun->RegisterComponent();
	AddInstanceComponent(Gun);
	return Gun;
}

{
	Shown = Clip;
	Figure->PlayAnimation(SupercutFigure::Clip(Clip), SupercutFigure::IsLoop(Clip));
	Figure->SetPosition(0.f, false);
	Figure->SetPlayRate(1.f);
}

2. **Open props: block walking, not shots or sight.** Chairs and ladders are frames you can see and shoot through; their JSON says so in `notes`. A full box round a ladder would stop bullets in thin air, and calling a chair cover would lie to the player. So the catalogue line gets one more key, `open=0|1`:
   - `blocks=1 open=0`: a full box, as specified before. Stops the player, enemies, shots and sight. Cover.
   - `blocks=1 open=1`: stops walking bodies only (the player and enemies). Shots, enemy sight and aim pass through as if it were not there. Never cover. No wall marks or impact effects on its box, since nothing hits it.
   - `blocks=0`: nothing, as before.
   Set `open=1` from the JSON when its `notes` say the prop is see-through, and for the categories `chair` and `ladder` unless the JSON says otherwise; write in your handoff which props got it and by which rule. Add a test: a shot and an enemy's sight check pass through an open prop that stops a walking body.

# Contact sheet of every T_*_BC.png in a batch folder, plus a hue census for the game's signal colours.
# Usage: python -I tex_sheet.py <batch folder> <out.jpg>
import colorsys, glob, os, sys
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw
src, out = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
files = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(src, "T_*_BC.png")))
cell = 320
sheet = Image.new("RGB", (cell * 4, (cell + 20) * ((len(files) + 3) // 4)), (40, 40, 40))
d = ImageDraw.Draw(sheet)
for i, f in enumerate(files):
    im = Image.open(f).convert("RGB")
    small = im.resize((cell, cell))
    x, y = (i % 4) * cell, (i // 4) * (cell + 20)
    sheet.paste(small, (x, y + 20))
    d.text((x + 4, y + 4), os.path.basename(f), fill=(255, 255, 255))
    px = im.resize((256, 256)).getdata()
    sig = {"yellow": 0, "red-orange": 0, "green": 0, "cyan": 0}
    for r, g, b in px:
        h, s, v = colorsys.rgb_to_hsv(r / 255, g / 255, b / 255)
        if s < 0.35 or v < 0.25:
            continue
        deg = h * 360
        if 40 <= deg < 70: sig["yellow"] += 1
        elif deg < 40 or deg >= 345: sig["red-orange"] += 1
        elif 80 <= deg < 160: sig["green"] += 1
        elif 160 <= deg < 200: sig["cyan"] += 1
    n = len(px)
    print(os.path.basename(f), " ".join("%s %.1f%%" % (k, 100 * v / n) for k, v in sig.items()))
sheet.save(out, quality=85)

UStaticMeshComponent* SupercutShapes::AddSetProp(AActor* Owner, USceneComponent* Parent, const FSetProp& Prop, const FVector& Location, const FRotator& Rotation, float Scale)
{
	check(Owner && Parent && Scale > 0.f);
	UStaticMesh* Mesh = SetPropMesh(Prop);
	UStaticMeshComponent* Part = NewObject<UStaticMeshComponent>(Owner);
	Part->SetMobility(EComponentMobility::Static);
	Part->SetStaticMesh(Mesh);
	Part->SetCollisionProfileName(TEXT("NoCollision"));
	Part->SetCanEverAffectNavigation(false);
	Part->SetupAttachment(Parent);
	Part->SetRelativeLocationAndRotation(Location, Rotation);
	Part->SetRelativeScale3D(FVector(Scale));
	Part->RegisterComponent();
	Owner->AddInstanceComponent(Part);
	if (Prop.Kind == ESetPropKind::Gear)
	{
		// The box round the mesh, in the mesh's own space, so it turns and scales with it.
		const FBox Local = Mesh->GetBoundingBox();
		UBoxComponent* Box = NewObject<UBoxComponent>(Owner);
		Box->SetMobility(EComponentMobility::Static);
		Box->SetCollisionProfileName(TEXT("BlockAll"));
		Box->SetCanEverAffectNavigation(false);
		Box->SetupAttachment(Part);
		Box->SetRelativeLocation(Local.GetCenter());
		Box->SetBoxExtent(Local.GetExtent(), false);
		Box->RegisterComponent();
		Owner->AddInstanceComponent(Box);
	}
	return Part;
}

## Five-minute start (from c4, Git Bash)

The commands below use `[pc-b]`; `[pc-c]` and `pc2` take the same commands (on pc2 add `-TimeoutSeconds 900` to `run`).
Pick a name for your lane (letters, digits, no spaces): use your lane name, for example `vfx1`. Never use another
lane's name and never `proof` (the farm's own check).

```bash
F="[notes]/unreal/megajam-2026/farm/farm.sh"
LOGS=/d/UE/wt/vfx1_farmlogs          # any folder on c4 outside the worktree; each step writes LOGS/<step>/

"$F" status [pc-b]                                   # 1. load check, see "Before a heavy step" below
"$F" mirror [pc-b] vfx1 /d/UE/wt/vfx1                 # 2. copy your worktree (changed files only)
"$F" build  [pc-b] vfx1 "$LOGS" -Jobs 8               # 3. SupercutEditor, Development
"$F" test   [pc-b] vfx1 "$LOGS"                       # 4. all Supercut tests (or: -Filter Supercut.Rooms)
"$F" package [pc-b] vfx1 "$LOGS"                      # 5. Development package (compiles the game target itself)
"$F" run    [pc-b] vfx1 "$LOGS" -Packaged -Exe '{B}\Supercut59\Windows\Supercut.exe' \
            -Run main8 -Seed 1 -Script '{P}\Script\main8.txt' -FixedFps 240 -Silent      # 6. scripted run
grep "RUN wrapped" "$LOGS/run/run.log"                # 7. compare with the reference line
```

- Extra words after the log folder go to the project's own script: `build` takes `build.ps1` arguments

  `run_demo.ps1` arguments. In them `{P}` is your mirror folder on the PC, `{B}` your packages folder, `{O}` the
  step's log folder. The run step adds `-Log` and `-Shots` (into its log folder) unless you give them.
- `package-shipping` builds the Shipping package to `{B}\Supercut59_ship\Windows`.

bool ASupercutEnemy::CanSee(const AActor* TargetActor, float Range, float LookHeight) const
{
	const FVector Here = GetActorLocation();
	const FVector There = TargetActor->GetActorLocation();
	if (FVector::Dist2D(Here, There) > Range)
	{
		return false;
	}
	FCollisionQueryParams Params(SCENE_QUERY_STAT(SupercutEnemySight), false, this);
	Params.AddIgnoredActor(TargetActor);
	return !GetWorld()->LineTraceTestByChannel(Here + FVector(0.f, 0.f, LookHeight), There + FVector(0.f, 0.f, 30.f), ECC_Visibility, Params);
}

### Sat 14 Nov 19:34:05 · Agent (claude-opus-5-5)

I'm writing a small gated helper for the [pc-c] steps. It waits until there's no game, no other lane's editor, CPU under 60% and at least 6 GB free, and only then mirrors, builds and tests.

**Sat 14 Nov 19:34:11 · Tool call: Bash** (Write a gated [pc-c] test helper)

```
cat > "[notes]/unreal/megajam-2026/lanes/props1/tools2/[pc-c]_test.sh" <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Mirror, build and test props1 on [pc-c], but only after FARM.md's load check passes (no Supercut, no UnrealEditor,
# no compiler, CPU under 60, 6 GB free). Waits up to about 9 minutes, then gives up with exit 9.
# Usage: [pc-c]_test.sh <log label> [test args]
F="[notes]/unreal/megajam-2026/farm/farm.sh"
LOGS=/d/UE/wt/props1_farmlogs/$1; shift
for i in $(seq 1 12); do
  S=$("$F" status [pc-c] 2>&1)
  C=$(echo "$S" | grep -o "cpu_load_pct=[0-9]*" | cut -d= -f2)
  R=$(echo "$S" | grep -o "free_ram_gb=[0-9]*" | cut -d= -f2)
  B=$(echo "$S" | grep busy_procs)
  echo "$(date +%H:%M:%S) [pc-c] cpu=$C ram=$R $B"
  if [ "${C:-100}" -lt 60 ] && [ "${R:-0}" -ge 6 ] && ! echo "$B" | grep -q -E "Supercut|UnrealEditor|clx"; then
    "$F" mirror [pc-c] props1 /d/UE/wt/props1 2>&1 | tail -1 || exit 1
    "$F" build [pc-c] props1 "$LOGS" -Jobs 8 2>&1 | tail -1
    grep -h -E "error C" "$LOGS"/build/*.log 2>/dev/null | head -5
    "$F" test [pc-c] props1 "$LOGS" "$@" 2>&1 | tail -2
    grep -o "PROPS catalogue: [0-9]* props" "$LOGS/test/tests.log" | head -1
    grep -E "Result=\{Fail" "$LOGS/test/tests.log" | sed 's/.*Name=/FAILED Name=/'
    exit 0
  fi
  sleep 45
done
echo "[pc-c] stayed busy"; exit 9
EOF
echo ok
```

cell = 320
sheet = Image.new("RGB", (cell * 4, (cell + 20) * ((len(files) + 3) // 4)), (40, 40, 40))
d = ImageDraw.Draw(sheet)
for i, f in enumerate(files):
    im = Image.open(f).convert("RGB")
    small = im.resize((cell, cell))
    x, y = (i % 4) * cell, (i // 4) * (cell + 20)
    sheet.paste(small, (x, y + 20))
    d.text((x + 4, y + 4), os.path.basename(f), fill=(255, 255, 255))

- `mirror` sends only files whose size or time differ, keeps file times (so builds stay incremental), never sends
  `Intermediate`, `Binaries`, `Saved`, `DerivedDataCache` or `.git`, and deletes files under `Source`, `Content`,
  `Config`, `Tools` and `Script` that are gone on c4. Files elsewhere in the mirror (`Art`, `Audio`) are never deleted.
  It mirrors whatever is in the folder you give it, committed or not. It does not commit, pull or push.

void ASupercutPlayerController::CountFrame()
{
	// Skip the first seconds: the map has just loaded and shaders are still arriving.
	const float FrameSeconds = FApp::GetDeltaTime();
	FpsClock += FrameSeconds;
	if (FpsClock < 3.f || bScriptOver)
	{
		return;
	}
	(USupercutTime::Get(this).IsFrozen() ? FrozenFrames : RollingFrames).Add(FrameSeconds);
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Mirror, build and test props1 on [pc-c], but only after FARM.md's load check passes (no Supercut, no UnrealEditor,
# no compiler, CPU under 60, 6 GB free). Waits up to about 9 minutes, then gives up with exit 9.
# Usage: [pc-c]_test.sh <log label> [test args]
F="[notes]/unreal/megajam-2026/farm/farm.sh"
LOGS=/d/UE/wt/props1_farmlogs/$1; shift
for i in $(seq 1 12); do
  S=$("$F" status [pc-c] 2>&1)
  C=$(echo "$S" | grep -o "cpu_load_pct=[0-9]*" | cut -d= -f2)
  R=$(echo "$S" | grep -o "free_ram_gb=[0-9]*" | cut -d= -f2)
  B=$(echo "$S" | grep busy_procs)
  echo "$(date +%H:%M:%S) [pc-c] cpu=$C ram=$R $B"
  if [ "${C:-100}" -lt 60 ] && [ "${R:-0}" -ge 6 ] && ! echo "$B" | grep -q -E "Supercut|UnrealEditor|clx"; then
    "$F" mirror [pc-c] props1 /d/UE/wt/props1 2>&1 | tail -1 || exit 1
    "$F" build [pc-c] props1 "$LOGS" -Jobs 8 2>&1 | tail -1
    grep -h -E "error C" "$LOGS"/build/*.log 2>/dev/null | head -5
    "$F" test [pc-c] props1 "$LOGS" "$@" 2>&1 | tail -2
    grep -o "PROPS catalogue: [0-9]* props" "$LOGS/test/tests.log" | head -1
    grep -E "Result=\{Fail" "$LOGS/test/tests.log" | sed 's/.*Name=/FAILED Name=/'
    exit 0
  fi
  sleep 45
done
echo "[pc-c] stayed busy"; exit 9

## Megascans against setC's props (swap or keep)

- **Sandbags: swap.** setC's SM_SandbagPile reads as black plastic bags in a low heap. SM_SandbagHeap is a crisp canvas
  scan stacked to 59 cm. Use the Megascans one; keep setC's SM_SandbagSaddleStack (a different shape).
- **Pallets: keep both.** setC's built pallet is clean and regular; SM_PalletOld and SM_PalletEuro have broken boards
  and real wear and look better within 2 m. Mix them; the euro pallet is a second shape.
- **Wooden crate: keep both.** Different objects. setC's SM_WoodenCrate is a closed 94 cm shipping crate (cover);
  SM_CrateSlatted is a 41 cm open fruit crate (small), stacked to 95 cm in SM_CrateSlattedStack.
- **Cable reel: keep both.** setC's SM_CableDrumBig (100 cm) has cable wound on it and reads as film kit. The Megascans
  reel (80 cm) is empty and sharper. Use both sizes.
- **Paint: keep both.** setC's SM_PaintCans are metal tins; SM_PaintBucket is a crusted plastic bucket, upright and tipped.
- **Drums and crates: keep both** for variety: setC's blue SM_SteelDrum against the grey rusty SM_DrumRusty, setC's
  dark plastic crate stack against the pale scanned crates. SM_JerseyBarrier is a 5.4 m long barrier, not a swap for
  setC's 1.6 m SM_ConcreteBlock.

## Hall textures

- **Swapped: T_Hall_Roof** (row 5, corrugated metal sheet). `out/batch4/textures/` has the same three names and
  channels as hall1's set. The scan is 2 x 2 m, packed 2 x 2 into the 2048 so on the roof panel's 400 cm repeat the ribs
  keep their real 15 cm pitch (hall1's set showed fine 7 cm ribs from a 200 cm scan stretched to 400). Metallic now
  comes from the scan (mean 0.72; hall1's was 0). Rust desaturated; base colour mean matched to hall1's set (gain 1.23).
  Re-import over the existing T_Hall_Roof assets; no mesh change.
- **Kept: T_Hall_Concrete.** Row 1 (industrial concrete floor) packed 2 x 2 on the 400 cm floor repeat shows four big
  bright blotches per cell, a visible grid on a big floor. Packed 1 x 1 the blotches get bigger. hall1's floor reads
  better at that repeat. Row 23 (stained concrete) is in `textures_extra` as a spare.
- **Kept: T_Hall_Wall.** Row 24 (dirty painted concrete wall) has a scuff band at floor level and formwork lines; on the
  200 cm wall repeat that band would repeat at 2 m up a 4 m panel. Its roughness map is 0.25 (glossy paint). Row 6 is
  plain white paint and would need the same darke
