Run it after the catalogue changes: python -I Tools/make_props_show.py\nimport os\n\nROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))\nCATALOGUE = os.path.join(ROOT, \"Content\", \"Props\", \"catalogue.txt\")\nROOM = os.path.join(ROOT, \"Content\", \"Rooms\", \"tests\", \"props_show.txt\")\nSCRIPT = os.path.join(ROOT, \"Script\", \"props1_show.txt\")\n\nGAP = 60           # cm between two props in a row\nAISLE = 300        # cm between two rows\nROW_WIDTH = 2400   # a row longer than this goes on in a new row\nWALK = 600         # cm/s, FSupercutTuning WalkSpeed\n\n\ndef read_catalogue():\n    props = []\n    for line in open(CATALOGUE, encoding=\"utf-8\"):\n        words = line.split()\n        if not words or words[0] != \"prop\":\n            continue\n        d = dict(w.split(\"=\", 1) for w in words[1:])\n        size = [float(v) for v in d[\"size\"].split(\",\")]\n        low = [float(v) for v in d[\"from\"].split(\",\")] if \"from\" in d else [-size[0] / 2, -size[1] / 2, 0.0]\n        props.append({\"name\": d[\"name\"], \"category\": d[\"category\"], \"size\": size, \"from\": low})\n    return props\n\n\ndef rows_of(props):\n    by_category = {}\n    for p in props:\n        by_category.setdefault(p[\"category\"], []).append(p)\n    # Low rows in front, tall rows behind, the hall pieces last.\n    order = sorted(by_category, key=lambda c: (c == \"hall_piece\", max(p[\"size\"][2] for p in by_category[c]), c))\n    rows = []\n    for category in order:\n        row, width = [], 0.0\n        for p in sorted(by_category[category], key=lambda p: (p[\"size\"][1], p[\"name\"])):\n            if row and width + p[\"size\"][1] > ROW_WIDTH:\n                rows.append((category, row))\n                row, width = [], 0.0\n            row.append(p)\n            width += p[\"size\"][1] + GAP\n        rows.append((category, row))\n    return rows\n\n\ndef main():\n    rows = rows_of(read_catalogue())\n    half = max(sum(p[\"size\"][1] + GAP for p in row) for _, row in rows) / 2\n    lines, centres = [], []\n    x = 0.0\n    for category, row in rows:\n        depth = max(p[\"size\"][0] for p in row)\n        width = sum(p[\"size\"][1] + GAP for p in row) - GAP\n        y = -width / 2\n        lines.append(\"# %s\" % category)\n        lines.append(\"box role=metal from=%g,%g,0 to=%g,%g,180\" % (x + depth / 2 - 5, y - 50, x + depth / 2 + 5, y - 40))\n        for p in row:\n            # Origin so the prop's box starts at y and is centred on the row line, base on the floor (1 cm up for flat ones).\n            at_x = x + depth / 2 - p[\"from\"][0] - p[\"size\"][0] / 2\n            at_y = y - p[\"from\"][1]\n            at_z = -p[\"from\"][2] + (1 if p[\"size\"][2] < 1 else 0)\n            lines.append(\"dress name=%s at=%g,%g,%g turn=0,0,0\" % (p[\"name\"], round(at_x, 1), round(at_y, 1), round(at_z, 1)))\n            y += p[\"size\"][1] + GAP\n        centres.append((category, x + depth / 2))\n        x += depth + AISLE\n    length = x\n    aisle_y = -half - 400\n    head = [\n        \"# The show room (lane props1): every prop of Content/Props/catalogue.txt in rows by category, low rows in front,\",\n        \"# the hall pieces at the back, and a 180 cm dark post at the left end of each row for scale.\",\n        \"# Written by Tools/make_props_show.py from the catalogue: run it again after the catalogue changes, do not edit by hand.\",\n        \"# Walk along the aisle on the left (-y) to see each row from the side. Script/props1_show.txt takes the pictures.\",\n        \"start at=-400,%g,0 facing=0\" % aisle_y,\n        \"gate  at=%g,%g,0 facing=0\" % (length + 200, aisle_y),\n        \"fall  below=-350\",\n        \"box role=floor from=-800,%g,-50 to=%g,%g,0\" % (aisle_y - 400, length + 600, half + 400),\n    ]\n    with open(ROOM, \"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\", newline=\"\\r\\n\") as f:\n        f.write(\"\\n\".join(head + lines) + \"\\n\")\n\n    # The script: walk the aisle (+x), stop opposite each row, turn to it (+y) and take a picture.\n    t, pos = 0.5, -400.0\n    s = [\"# Pictures of the show room (lane props1). Written by Tools/make_props_show.py.\",\n         \"# Run: -Packaged -Room tests/props_show -Script <this file> -Silent -ResX 1920 -ResY 1080 -TimeoutSeconds 300\",\n         \"%.2f lookat %g,0,100\" % (t, length / 2), \"%.2f shot show_side_a\" % (t + 0.4)]\n    t += 1.0\n    for i, (category, cx) in enumerate(centres):\n        go = (cx - pos) / WALK\n        s.append(\"%.2f look 0 0\" % t)\n        s.append(\"%.2f move 1 0\" % (t + 0.05))\n        t += 0.05 + go\n        s.append(\"%.2f move 0 0\" % t)\n        s.append(\"%.2f look 90 -12\" % (t + 0.4))\n        s.append(\"%.2f shot row%02d_%s\" % (t + 0.9, i, category))\n        t += 1.2\n        pos = cx\n    end = length + 100\n    s.append(\"%.2f look 0 0\" % t)\n    s.append(\"%.2f move 1 0\" % (t + 0.05))\n    t += 0.05 + (end - pos) / WALK\n    s.append(\"%.2f move 0 0\" % t)\n    s.append(\"%.2f lookat %g,0,100\" % (t + 0.4, length / 2))\n    s.append(\"%.2f shot show_side_b\" % (t + 0.9))\n    s.append(\"%.2f end\" % (t + 1.5))\n    with open(SCRIPT, \"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\", newline=\"\\r\\n\") as f:\n        f.write(\"\\n\".join(s) + \"\\n\")\n    print(\"%d rows, %d props, room %g x %g cm, script %.1f s\" % (len(rows), sum(len(r) for _, r in rows), length, 2 * half, t + 1.5))\n\n\nmain()\n"

**Sat 14 Nov 20:58:43 · Tool call: Bash** (Write a read-only mesh measuring script)

```
mkdir -p /d/UE/wt/props1_farmlogs/py; cat > /d/UE/wt/props1_farmlogs/py/measure_led.py <<'EOF'
# Read-only: measures SM_LightLEDPanel's vertices to find its lamp head (lane props1).
import unreal
mesh = unreal.load_asset("/Game/Props/Real/SM_LightLEDPanel")
desc = mesh.get_static_mesh_description(0)
pts = [desc.get_vertex_position(unreal.VertexID(i)) for i in range(desc.get_vertex_count())]
zmax = max(p.z for p in pts)
for cut in (0.75, 0.6):
    head = [p for p in pts if p.z > zmax * cut]
    lo = [min(getattr(p, a) for p in head) for a in "xyz"]
    hi = [max(getattr(p, a) for p in head) for a in "xyz"]
    unreal.log("SUPERCUT measure: above %.0f%% of %.1f cm: %d vertices, x %.1f..%.1f y %.1f..%.1f z %.1f..%.1f" % (cut * 100, zmax, len(head), lo[0], hi[0], lo[1], hi[1], lo[2], hi[2]))
# Depth profile of the head along x: how many vertices sit near each x, to find the flat front face.
head = [p for p in pts if p.z > zmax * 0.6]
xs = sorted(p.x for p in head)
for x0 in range(int(xs[0]) - 1, int(xs[-1]) + 2, 4):
    n = sum(1 for x in xs if x0 <= x < x0 + 4)
    if n:
        unreal.log("SUPERCUT measure: x %d..%d: %d" % (x0, x0 + 4, n))
EOF
echo ok
```

**Sat 14 Nov 21:06:22 · Tool call: Bash** (Write the roof re-import script and check c4 editors and RAM)

```
mkdir -p "[notes]/unreal/megajam-2026/lanes/props1/tools2"; cat > "[notes]/unreal/megajam-2026/lanes/props1/tools2/reimport_roof.py" <<'EOF'
# One-off (lane props1, mega1 batch4): re-import Art/props_real/hall1/textures/T_Hall_Roof_{BC,N,ORM}.png over the
# existing /Game/Props/Real/Textures/T_Hall_Roof_* assets in place. No new asset, no material change: the settings each
# texture had before (sRGB, compression, LOD group, green flip, max size) are put back after the import.
import os
import unreal

ROOT = unreal.Paths.convert_relative_path_to_full(unreal.Paths.project_dir())
SOURCE = os.path.join(ROOT, "Art", "props_real", "hall1", "textures")
TEXTURES = "/Game/Props/Real/Textures"
EAL = unreal.EditorAssetLibrary
TOOLS = unreal.AssetToolsHelpers.get_asset_tools()
KEYS = ["srgb", "compression_settings", "lod_group", "flip_green_channel", "max_texture_size"]


def log(text):
    unreal.log("SUPERCUT reimport_roof: " + text)


for kind in ("BC", "N", "ORM"):
    name = "T_Hall_Roof_" + kind
    path = TEXTURES + "/" + name
    before = unreal.load_asset(path)
    if not isinstance(before, unreal.Texture2D):
        raise RuntimeError(path + " is not an existing Texture2D")
    settings = {k: before.get_editor_property(k) for k in KEYS}
    old_size = (before.blueprint_get_size_x(), before.blueprint_get_size_y())
    task = unreal.AssetImportTask()
    task.set_editor_property("filename", os.path.join(SOURCE, name + ".png"))
    task.set_editor_property("destination_path", TEXTURES)
    task.set_editor_property("destination_name", name)
    task.set_editor_property("automated", True)
    task.set_editor_property("replace_existing", True)
    task.set_editor_property("replace_existing_settings", False)
    task.set_editor_property("save", False)
    TOOLS.import_asset_tasks([task])
    after = unreal.load_asset(path)
    if after != before:
        raise RuntimeError(name + ": the import made a new object instead of replacing the old one")
    for k, v in settings.items():
        after.set_editor_property(k, v)
    if not EAL.save_loaded_asset(after, False):
        raise RuntimeError(name + " not saved")
    log("%s re-imported in place: %s -> %dx%d, %s" % (name, old_size, after.blueprint_get_size_x(), after.blueprint_get_size_y(),
        ", ".join("%s=%s" % (k, after.get_editor_property(k)) for k in KEYS)))

mi = unreal.load_asset("/Game/Props/Real/Materials/MI_Hall_Roof")
for p in mi.get_editor_property("texture_parameter_values"):
    log("MI_Hall_Roof %s = %s" % (p.parameter_info.name, p.parameter_value.get_path_name()))
log("done")
EOF

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- Room files

IMPLEMENT_SIMPLE_AUTOMATION_TEST(FSupercutSoundstageTest, "Supercut.Rooms.SoundstageFileBuildsTheSamePiecesAsTheOldCode", RunTestFlags)
bool FSupercutSoundstageTest::RunTest(const FString& Parameters)
{
	FRunTestWorld World;
	if (!TestTrue(TEXT("test world starts"), World.Start()))
	{
		return false;
	}
	// The fixture was first written by the last build that still built the test room in C++ (commit 3c28e43).
	// The light pass rewrote it: the desk lamp, the fill and the studio walls are in it with the default tuning,
	// so a change to a default of the Light or Signal colours section needs the fixture written again. The props pass
	// added the lamp's mesh (SM_Lamp) and its glowing bulb and changed no other line.
	const FString FixtureFile = FPaths::Combine(FPaths::GameSourceDir(), TEXT("Supercut/SupercutTestRoomPieces.txt"));
	TArray<FString> Before;
	if (!TestTrue(TEXT("the fixture is read"), FFileHelper::LoadFileToStringArray(Before, *FixtureFile)))
	{
		return false;
	}
	Before.RemoveAll([](const FString& Line) { return Line.IsEmpty(); });

	World.Run().Begin({ TEXT("soundstage") }, 1);
	const TArray<FString> Now = DescribeRoom(World.GetTestWorld());

	TestEqual(TEXT("the same number of pieces"), Now.Num(), Before.Num());
	TestEqual(TEXT("the fixture holds 54 pieces"), Before.Num(), 54);
	int32 Different = 0;
	for (int32 Index = 0; Index < FMath::Min(Now.Num(), Before.Num()); ++Index)
	{
		if (Now[Index] != Before[Index])
		{
			++Different;
			AddError(FString::Printf(TEXT("piece %d differs. Old code: [%s] Room file: [%s]"), Index, *Before[Index], *Now[Index]));
		}
	}
	TestEqual(TEXT("no piece differs"), Different, 0);
	TestEqual(TEXT("the fall line is where the old kill height was"), World.Run().GetRoom()->GetFallHeight(), -350.f);
	return true;
}

# Read-only: measures SM_LightLEDPanel's vertices to find its lamp head (lane props1).
import unreal
mesh = unreal.load_asset("/Game/Props/Real/SM_LightLEDPanel")
desc = mesh.get_static_mesh_description(0)
pts = [desc.get_vertex_position(unreal.VertexID(i)) for i in range(desc.get_vertex_count())]
zmax = max(p.z for p in pts)
for cut in (0.75, 0.6):
    head = [p for p in pts if p.z > zmax * cut]
    lo = [min(getattr(p, a) for p in head) for a in "xyz"]
    hi = [max(getattr(p, a) for p in head) for a in "xyz"]
    unreal.log("SUPERCUT measure: above %.0f%% of %.1f cm: %d vertices, x %.1f..%.1f y %.1f..%.1f z %.1f..%.1f" % (cut * 100, zmax, len(head), lo[0], hi[0], lo[1], hi[1], lo[2], hi[2]))
# Depth profile of the head along x: how many vertices sit near each x, to find the flat front face.
head = [p for p in pts if p.z > zmax * 0.6]
xs = sorted(p.x for p in head)
for x0 in range(int(xs[0]) - 1, int(xs[-1]) + 2, 4):
    n = sum(1 for x in xs if x0 <= x < x0 + 4)
    if n:
        unreal.log("SUPERCUT measure: x %d..%d: %d" % (x0, x0 + 4, n))
```

# Read-only: the revolver body's and enemy pistols' bounds, and the revolver's grip by height slices (lane props1).
import unreal
def pts_of(path):
    desc = unreal.load_asset(path).get_static_mesh_description(0)
    return [desc.get_vertex_position(unreal.VertexID(i)) for i in range(desc.get_vertex_count())]
def box(pts):
    return " ".join("%s %.2f..%.2f" % (a, min(getattr(p, a) for p in pts), max(getattr(p, a) for p in pts)) for a in "xyz")
for path in ("/Game/Props/Held/SM_Revolver_Body", "/Game/Props/Held/SM_Revolver_Cylinder", "/Game/Props/SM_EnemyPistol", "/Game/Props/SM_EnemyPistol_Long"):
    unreal.log("SUPERCUT measure: %s %s" % (path, box(pts_of(path))))
pts = pts_of("/Game/Props/Held/SM_Revolver_Body")
z0, z1 = min(p.z for p in pts), max(p.z for p in pts)
z = z0
while z < z1:
    s = [p for p in pts if z <= p.z < z + 1.0]
    if s:
        unreal.log("SUPERCUT measure: body z %.1f..%.1f: %d vertices, %s" % (z, z + 1, len(s), box(s)))
    z += 1.0
EOF

IMPLEMENT_SIMPLE_AUTOMATION_TEST(FSupercutFigureGruntClipsTest, "Supercut.Figures.GruntStatesShowTheirClips", FigureTestFlags)
bool FSupercutFigureGruntClipsTest::RunTest(const FString& Parameters)
{
	FFigureTestWorld World;
	if (!TestTrue(TEXT("test world starts"), World.Start()))
	{
		return false;
	}
	const FSupercutTuning& Tuning = FSupercutTuning::Get();
	ASupercutCharacter* Player = World.Spawn<ASupercutCharacter>(FVector::ZeroVector);
	ASupercutGrunt* Grunt = World.Spawn<ASupercutGrunt>(FVector(1000.f, 0.f, 0.f), FRotator(0.f, 180.f, 0.f));

import json, glob, collections
keys = collections.Counter()
lic = collections.Counter()
for f in glob.glob("*/**/*.json", recursive=True):
    try:
        d = json.load(open(f, encoding="utf-8"))
    except Exception as e:
        print("bad", f, e); continue

EOF

I'll generate the sourced-assets table with a script from the JSONs, so it matches what is actually in the catalogue:

**Sat 14 Nov 21:16:01 · Tool call: Bash** (Write and try the sourced-assets list script)

```
cat > "[notes]/unreal/megajam-2026/lanes/props1/tools2/sourced_list.py" <<'EOF'
# Lane props1: prints the sourced-assets table (markdown) for every prop in the catalogue, from each prop's JSON in
# Art/props_real. Run: python -I sourced_list.py D:/UE/wt/props1
import glob, json, os, sys

root = sys.argv[1]
by_mesh = {}
for f in glob.glob(os.path.join(root, "Art", "props_real", "*", "**", "*.json"), recursive=True):
    d = json.load(open(f, encoding="utf-8"))
    if isinstance(d, dict) and "licence" in d:
        lane = os.path.relpath(f, os.path.join(root, "Art", "props_real")).split(os.sep)[0]
        by_mesh.setdefault("SM_" + os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(f))[0].removeprefix("SM_"), (lane, d))
rows, missing = [], []
for line in open(os.path.join(root, "Content", "Props", "catalogue.txt"), encoding="utf-8"):
    w = line.split()
    if not w or w[0] != "prop":
        continue
    kv = dict(x.split("=", 1) for x in w[1:])
    hit = by_mesh.get(kv["mesh"])
    if not hit:
        missing.append(kv["mesh"]); continue
    lane, d = hit
    src = d.get("source", "")
    item = d.get("megascans_item", "")
    page = d.get("megascans_page", "")
    lic = " ".join(str(d["licence"]).split()).replace("|", "/")
    rows.append((kv["name"], kv["mesh"], lane, src, (item + " " + page).strip(), lic))
print("| Prop | Mesh | Lane | Source | Megascans item and page | Licence and author (from the prop's JSON) |")
print("|---|---|---|---|---|---|")
for r in rows:
    print("| " + " | ".join(r) + " |")
print("\n%d props, missing JSON: %s" % (len(rows), missing or "none"))
EOF
cd "[notes]/unreal/megajam-2026/lanes/props1/tools2"; python -I sourced_list.py D:/UE/wt/props1 | tail -3; python -I sourced_list.py D:/UE/wt/props1 | awk -F'|' '{print $5}' | sort | uniq -c
```

```
cd "[notes]/unreal/megajam-2026/lanes/props1"; python -I - <<'EOF'
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw
import glob, os, re
src = r"D:/UE/wt/props1_farmlogs/show1_shots/run/shots"
names = sorted((os.path.basename(p)[:-4] for p in glob.glob(src + "/row*.png")), key=lambda n: tuple(int(x) for x in re.findall(r"\d+", n)))
W, H, C = 640, 360, 3
for s in range(0, len(names), 12):
    chunk = names[s:s + 12]
    sheet = Image.new("RGB", (W * C, H * ((len(chunk) + C - 1) // C)))
    for i, n in enumerate(chunk):
        im = Image.open(os.path.join(src, n + ".png")).convert("RGB").resize((W, H))
        d = ImageDraw.Draw(im); d.rectangle((0, 0, 110, 22), fill=(0, 0, 0)); d.text((5, 5), n, fill=(255, 255, 255))
        sheet.paste(im, ((i % C) * W, (i // C) * H))
    sheet.save("tmp/rows_%d.jpg" % (s // 12), quality=82)
    print("tmp/rows_%d.jpg" % (s // 12), chunk[0], chunk[-1])
EOF
```

# Lane props1, the AFTER pass on [pc-c], one step at a time, each after the load check: package the props1 tree, then
# the 8 entry views with frame times, the show room entry frame times, the show room pictures, the close-up, the
# enemies' revolver, and main8 twice. Logs land in /d/UE/wt/props1_farmlogs/<label>_*.
# Usage: [pc-c]_after.sh <label>     (run [pc-c]_test.sh first: this mirrors nothing)
T="$(dirname "$0")"; F="[notes]/unreal/megajam-2026/farm/farm.sh"
L=/d/UE/wt/props1_farmlogs/$1
EXE='{B}\Supercut59\Windows\Supercut.exe'
gate() { bash "$T/[pc-c]_wait.sh" | tail -1 | grep -q READY || { echo "[pc-c] busy, stopped before $1"; exit 9; }; }
gate package
"$F" package [pc-c] props1 "$L" 2>&1 | tail -1
grep -E "BUILD SUCC|BUILD FAIL" "$L/package/package_run.log" || { echo "package failed"; exit 1; }
bash "$T/[pc-c]_entries.sh" "$1" fight/01_wind_machine fight/02_stunt_run fight/03_long_lens fight/04_hot_set fight/05_martini_shot puzzle/a_the_cue puzzle/b_the_wild_wall puzzle/c_the_cutaway tests/props_show || exit 9
shoot() {   # <name> <room> <script> <timeout>
  gate "$1"
  "$F" run [pc-c] props1 "${L}_$1" -Packaged -Exe "$EXE" -Room "$2" -Script "{P}\\Script\\$3" -Silent -ResX 1920 -ResY 1080 -FixedFps 60 -TimeoutSeconds "$4" 2>&1 | tail -1
  echo "$1: $(ls "${L}_$1"/run/shots | wc -l) pictures, $(grep -c 'Fatal error' "${L}_$1"/run/run.log) fatal"
}
shoot show tests/props_show props1_show.txt 400
shoot close tests/props_show props1_close.txt 120
shoot enemy tests/props1_enemy props1_enemy.txt 120
for N in 1 2; do
  gate "main8 $N"
  "$F" run [pc-c] props1 "${L}_main8_$N" -Packaged -Exe "$EXE" -Run main8 -Seed 1 -Script '{P}\Script\main8.txt' -FixedFps 240 -Silent -TimeoutSeconds 600 2>&1 | tail -1
  echo "main8 $N: $(grep -h -o 'RUN wrapped.*' "${L}_main8_$N"/run/run.log)"
done
EOF
echo ok

```
# Imports the realistic props the prop lanes deliver, and writes the catalogue the game and the level generator read.
#
# Source: every Art/props_real/<lane>/<batch>/SM_<Name>.fbx with its SM_<Name>.json and three textures
# T_<Name>_BC.png (base colour), T_<Name>_N.png (DirectX normal) and T_<Name>_ORM.png (occlusion, roughness, metallic),
# in the delivery format of unreal/megajam-2026/lanes/PROPS_REALISTIC_SPEC.md.
# Made here, in /Game/Props/Real:
#   SM_<Name>                    the mesh, no collision (the game gives a blocking prop a box from its catalogue size)
#   Textures/T_<Set>_BC, _N, _ORM one texture set per prop, or one per shared set (same_textures_as)
#   Materials/M_PropReal         the one master material; Materials/MI_<Set> one instance per texture set
# Hall pieces (lane hall1, Art/props_real/hall1/<batch>) differ: their JSON lists "materials" (slot names such as
# M_Hall_Concrete) and "textures" (per slot, files in Art/props_real/hall1/textures). Each slot name is one shared set
# (M_Hall_Concrete -> T_Hall_Concrete_*, MI_Hall_Concrete), assigned to the mesh by slot name. Their origin is a snap
# point, so their box comes from "bounds_cm".
# Written: Content/Props/catalogue.txt, one line per prop that passed the checks below.
#
# Safe to run again: a prop whose mesh already exists is not imported again and nothing of it is changed; a new batch
# folder is picked up. The catalogue is written from scratch every time. To redo one prop, delete its SM_, its MI_ and
# its textures (if no other prop shares them) and run again.
#
# Why a new script and not make_props.py: make_props.py deletes and remakes all of /Game/Props/Set on every run and

Part->RegisterComponent();
	Owner->AddInstanceComponent(Part);
	if (Prop.bBlocks && bSolid)
	{
		// The box stands in for the mesh in every query, as a box line of a room file would: a static, unseen mesh part,
		// so a shot leaves its wall mark on it and enemies do not move through it (the room lets enemies through box
		// components only, the old film gear).
		UStaticMeshComponent* Box = NewObject<UStaticMeshComponent>(Owner);
		Box->SetMobility(EComponentMobility::Static);
		Box->SetStaticMesh(SupercutShapes::Mesh(ESupercutShape::Cube));
		Box->SetVisibility(false);
		Box->SetCastShadow(false);
		Box->SetCanEverAffectNavigation(false);
		if (Prop.bOpen)
		{
			// Walking bodies (the player and enemies are Pawn) stop at it. Shots, chips, the aim and the Marksman's line
			// ask for WorldStatic, WorldDynamic and Pawn objects and enemy sight traces Visibility, so none of them meets it.
			Box->SetCollisionEnabled(ECollisionEnabled::QueryOnly);
			Box->SetCollisionObjectType(ECC_PhysicsBody);
			Box->SetCollisionResponseToAllChannels(ECR_Ignore);
			Box->SetCollisionResponseToChannel(ECC_Pawn, ECR_Block);
		}
		else
		{
			Box->SetCollisionProfileName(TEXT("BlockAll"));
		}
		Box->SetupAttachment(Part);
		Box->SetRelativeLocation(Prop.From + Prop.Size * 0.5);
		Box->SetRelativeScale3D(Prop.Size / 100.0);   // the cube is 100 cm round its centre
		Box->RegisterComponent();
		Owner->AddInstanceComponent(Box);
	}
	return Part;
}

void ASupercutRoom::BuildLight()
{
	const FSupercutTuning& Tuning = FSupercutTuning::Get();

	// The model: the box round every solid shape of the room. Everything below is placed from it.
	const FBox Model = GetComponentsBoundingBox();
	checkf(Model.IsValid, TEXT("Room %s has no solid shape, so there is no model to light"), *RoomName);
	const FVector Middle = Model.GetCenter();
	const float Radius = Model.GetExtent().Size();
	const FVector ToLamp = FRotator(Tuning.LampHeight, Tuning.LampSide, 0.f).Vector();
	const float Distance = Tuning.LampDistance * Radius;
	const FVector LampAt = Middle + ToLamp * Distance;

	// The desk lamp: one warm spot light with shadows, aimed at the middle. Its cone holds the whole model.
	USpotLightComponent* Lamp = NewObject<USpotLightComponent>(this);
	Lamp->SetMobility(EComponentMobility::Movable);
	Lamp->SetupAttachment(RootComponent);
	Lamp->SetRelativeLocationAndRotation(LampAt, (-ToLamp).Rotation());
	Lamp->IntensityUnits = ELightUnits::Candelas;
	Lamp->Intensity = Tuning.LampLux * FMath::Square(Distance / 100.f);   // candelas over metres squared is lux
	Lamp->bUseTemperature = true;
	Lamp->Temperature = Tuning.LampKelvin;
	Lamp->OuterConeAngle = FMath::Min(80.f, FMath::RadiansToDegrees(FMath::Asin(1.f / Tuning.LampDistance)) + 4.f);
	Lamp->InnerConeAngle = Lamp->OuterConeAngle - 4.f;
	Lamp->AttenuationRadius = Distance + Radius * 1.5f;
	Lamp->SourceRadius = Tuning.LampSoftness * Distance;
	Lamp->CastShadows = true;
	{
		FBox(FVector(Low.X - Thick, Low.Y, Low.Z), FVector(Low.X, High.Y, High.Z)),
		FBox(FVector(High.X, Low.Y, Low.Z), FVector(High.X + Thick, High.Y, High.Z)),
		FBox(FVector(Low.X, Low.Y - Thick, Low.Z), FVector(High.X, Low.Y, High.Z)),
		FBox(FVector(Low.X, High.Y, Low.Z), FVector(High.X, High.Y + Thick, High.Z)),
		FBox(FVector(Low.X, Low.Y, High.Z), FVector(High.X, High.Y, High.Z + Thick)),
	};
	for (const FBox& Slab : Slabs)
	{
		UStaticMeshComponent* Part = AddBox(Slab.Min, Slab.Max, Dark, false);
		Part->SetCastShadow(false);
		Part->SetAffectDistanceFieldLighting(false);
		Part->SetAffectDynamicIndirectLighting(false);
		SupercutShapes::MarkForSketch(Part, SupercutShapes::ESketch::Studio);
	}

# props1 HANDOFF: set props in SUPERCUT

Lane props1, 14 Nov 2026, c4, UE 5.9, repo `D:\UE\Projects\Supercut59`, branch `ue59`. Not pushed.

## What was built

- **13 set props imported.** `Art/props_gen` holds the FBX and base colour PNG of each (SOURCE.md names lanes rodin1,
  rodin2 and rodin3). `Tools/make_props.py` imports them all into `Content/Props/Set`: 13 static meshes, 13 textures
  (sRGB, default compression, World group), one material `M_SetProp` (ColorTex into Base Colour, Rough 0.8) and one
  instance per prop. No Nanite, no lightmap UVs, no collision in the asset. Triangles: 2,998 or 3,000 each, the lamp
  8,000. `Tools/make_figures.py` used to clear all of `/Game/Props`; it now clears only what it makes there.
- **The lamp in every room.** `ASupercutRoom::BuildLight` stands `SM_Lamp` on the desk (the model's lowest point) with
  its bulb at the desk light. Only its yaw turns (base flat on the desk), and one uniform scale (2.28 to 3.26 in the
  eight rooms) puts the bulb at the light's height. The lamp throws no shadow, so its shade cannot block the light.
  A glowing ball (M_Glow, the lamp's colour temperature, strength 3) sits over the mesh's own grey bulb. The light
  (position, rotation, candelas, cone, colour, softness) is not touched: the `LIGHT lamp at` lines of all 8 rooms are
  the same as before, and the soundstage fixture's light line is unchanged.
- **The `dress` line.** `dress name=<set prop> at=x,y,z turn=pitch,yaw,roll [scale=1]` places a set prop with the
  centre of its base at `at`. It is read like every other piece. An unknown name (the error lists the 13 names), the
  lamp, or a scale of 0 or less is refused with the file and line; a missing mesh stops the game with a fatal error
  that names the asset and the import script. Dress props are queued and built after the light, so they never move it.
- **Two kinds.** Desk things (ruler, pencil, glue, tape, set_square, knife) collide with nothing. Film gear (chair,
  film_light, camera, apple_boxes, sandbags, cable_reel) gets a BlockAll `UBoxComponent` round its mesh bounds; the
  mesh itself has no collision. No set prop has a sketch stencil mark, so the frozen sketch draws them like the rest

#pragma once

#include "CoreMinimal.h"

class USceneComponent;

/**
 * The realistic props: Content/Props/catalogue.txt, written by Tools/make_props_real.py from what the prop lanes
 * deliver, read here at game start. One line per prop, in the room files' key=value style:
 *
 *   prop name=road_case_single mesh=SM_RoadCaseSingle category=road_case class=cover blocks=1 size=68,109,85
 *
 * with from=x,y,z (the box's lowest corner, for hall pieces whose origin is a snap point) and lens=x,y,z tilt=degrees
 * (hall lights), end=x,y,z endyaw=degrees (dolly track: where the next piece starts and how it turns) and where=hall
 * (never in a room) where the prop has them. A prop with blocks=1 also has open=0 or open=1. A dress line of a room file
 * places a catalogue prop by its name. Whether a prop blocks comes only from here:
 *   blocks=1 open=0  a box of its size stops the player, enemies, shots and sight, like a box line of a room file
 *   blocks=1 open=1  a frame you see and shoot through (chairs, ladders): its box stops the player and enemies only
 *   blocks=0         nothing
 */
namespace SupercutProps
{
	struct FProp

		FVector From = FVector::ZeroVector;   // the box's lowest corner in the mesh's own space
		bool bHasLens = false;
		FVector Lens = FVector::ZeroVector;
		float Tilt = 0.f;
		bool bHasEnd = false;
		FVector End = FVector::ZeroVector;   // a dolly track's far end, where the next piece's origin goes
		float EndYaw = 0.f;                  // and how far the next piece turns
		bool bHallOnly = false;              // where=hall: green, the open-gate signal colour, so never in a room
	};

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Waits until [pc-c] passes FARM.md's load check (no Supercut, no UnrealEditor, no compiler, no AutomationTool (dotnet), no shader workers, CPU under 60, 6 GB free),
# then prints READY and exits 0. Gives up after about 15 minutes with exit 9. Run it right before each heavy step.
F="[notes]/unreal/megajam-2026/farm/farm.sh"
for i in $(seq 1 20); do
  S=$("$F" status [pc-c] 2>&1)
  C=$(echo "$S" | grep -o "cpu_load_pct=[0-9]*" | cut -d= -f2)
  R=$(echo "$S" | grep -o "free_ram_gb=[0-9]*" | cut -d= -f2)
  B=$(echo "$S" | grep -o "busy_procs=.*" | head -1)
  echo "$(date +%H:%M:%S) [pc-c] cpu=$C ram=$R $B"
  if [ "${C:-100}" -lt 60 ] && [ "${R:-0}" -ge 6 ] && ! echo "$B" | grep -q -E "Supercut|UnrealEditor|clx|dotnet|AutomationTool|ShaderCompile"; then
    echo READY; exit 0
  fi
  sleep 45
done
echo "[pc-c] stayed busy"; exit 9

def group_texture_sets(props):
    """Props that name the same texture set share one import of it, at the largest size any of them needs. Their
    delivered files must be byte for byte the same as the first prop's, or the prop is refused.
    Returns ({set: (files, max size)}, {stem: why refused})."""
    refused = {}
    first = {}
    for prop in props:
        for set_name, files in prop["sets"].items():
            if set_name not in first:
                first[set_name] = (files, prop["stem"])
                continue
            for kind in TEXTURE_KINDS:
                if files[kind] != first[set_name][0][kind] and md5(files[kind]) != md5(first[set_name][0][kind]):
                    refused[prop["stem"]] = "shares texture set %s but its %s differs from %s's" % (set_name, kind, first[set_name][1])
    sets = {}
    for prop in props:
        if prop["stem"] in refused:
            continue
        for set_name in prop["sets"]:
            size = SET_SIZE.get(set_name, MAX_SIZE[prop["data"]["size_class"]])
            sets[set_name] = (first[set_name][0], max(size, sets.get(set_name, (None, 0))[1]))
    return sets, refused

# Lane props1: cooked size per catalogue prop from UnrealPak's container listing.
# python -I cooked_sizes.py <worktree> <listing.csv>   prints a markdown table and totals.
# A prop's bytes: its mesh plus each texture set it uses (three textures and the MI). A set used by more than one prop
# is counted with each of them and named in the shared column, so the column does not add up; the totals line does.
import csv, glob, json, os, re, sys
root, listing = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
size = {}
with open(listing, newline="") as f:
    for row in csv.reader(f, skipinitialspace=True):
        if len(row) > 2 and "/Content/Props/" in row[0]:
            name = os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(row[0]))[0]
            size[name] = size.get(name, 0) + int(row[2])
props = {}
for line in open(os.path.join(root, "Content", "Props", "catalogue.txt"), encoding="utf-8"):
    m = re.match(r"prop name=(\S+) mesh=(\S+)", line)
    if m:
        props[m.group(2)] = m.group(1)
sets_of = {}
for path in glob.glob(os.path.join(root, "Art", "props_real", "*", "*", "*.json")):
    data = json.load(open(path, encoding="utf-8"))
    mesh = "SM_" + data["name"][3:] if data["name"].startswith("SM_") else "SM_" + data["name"]
    stem = mesh[3:]
    if "materials" in data:
        sets = [s[2:] for s in data["materials"]]
    elif data.get("same_textures_as"):
        sets = [data["same_textures_as"][2:-2]]
    else:
        sets = [stem]
    sets_of[mesh] = sets
users = {}
for mesh in props:
    for s in sets_of[mesh]:
        users.setdefault(s, []).append(mesh)
def set_bytes(s):
    return sum(size.get(n, 0) for n in ("T_%s_BC" % s, "T_%s_N" % s, "T_%s_ORM" % s, "MI_%s" % s))
print("| Prop | Mesh | Mesh KB | Texture sets KB | Total KB | Shares a set with |")
print("|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---|")
for mesh in sorted(props, key=lambda m: props[m]):
    m = size.get(mesh, 0)
    t = sum(set_bytes(s) for s in sets_of[mesh])
    shared = sorted({props[o] for s in sets_of[mesh] for o in users[s] if o != mesh})
    note = ", ".join(shared) if len(shared) <= 3 else "%d hall pieces" % len(shared)
    print("| %s | %s | %d | %d | %d | %s |" % (props[mesh], mesh, m / 1024, t / 1024, (m + t) / 1024, note))
meshes = sum(size.get(m, 0) for m in props)
sets = sum(set_bytes(s) for s in users)
allp = sum(size.values())
print("\nTotals: meshes %.1f MB, %d texture sets %.1f MB, everything under Content/Props %.1f MB (cooked, UnrealPak Size column)." % (meshes / 2**20, len(users), sets / 2**20, allp / 2**20))
missing = [m for m in props if m not in size]
print("Meshes not in the listing: %s" % (", ".join(missing) or "none"))
EOF
python -I "$T/cooked_sizes.py" D:/UE/wt/props1 D:/UE/wt/props1_farmlogs/props1_list.csv > /d/UE/wt/props1_farmlogs/cooked.md; tail -3 /d/UE/wt/props1_farmlogs/cooked.md; sort -t'|' -k6 -n -r /d/UE/wt/props1_farmlogs/cooked.md | head -5
```

Piped into `tail`, a failure is hidden and the old mirror runs.\n- UnrealPak lists the IoStore container with `UnrealPak.exe <utoc> -List -csv=<file>`; `-List=<utoc>` only prints\n  its usage.\n- `props1_entry.txt` is LF in the working copy; git turns it to CRLF. Harmless.\n- `Art/props_real` (FBX and PNG sources) lives in the game repo, not the dev log repo.\n\n## Sourced assets\n\nThe roof texture set, not on the table below (it has no prop JSON): **Corrugated Metal Sheet**, Quixel Megascans,\nhttps://www.fab.com/listings/109b6f59-253b-4a54-aa50-ade924223725, Fab Standard License. Used by `MI_Hall_Roof`.\n\nEvery Megascans prop ships in the game. Raw files, FBX and textures stay out of this repo.\n\nCOOKED_AND_SOURCED_TABLES\n"
}

### Sat 14 Nov 22:56:34 · Agent (claude-opus-5-5)

Lane props1 is finished. HANDOFF.md is written, and the props1 branch is clean at `b13facc`: 24 commits, not merged or pushed.

**What's in the branch**
- **Props:** 125 props from five prop lanes, read from a catalogue when the game starts. A missing prop or mesh stops the game with an error that names it.
- **Rooms:** the 8 rooms of main8 are dressed with catalogue film gear, and each room's lamp is now the LED panel prop.
- **Enemies:** both enemy types hold the player's revolver. Their shots still start where they did before.
- **Show room:** one test room holds all 125 props.
- **Hall roof:** it uses the Megascans corrugated metal textures.

**Checks**
- Build and tests on [pc-c]: 122 of 122 pass.
- main8 from a package, run twice: both runs gave `RUN wrapped: takes 1, time 98.2 s, shots 46, freezes 14, kills 17`, matching the reference.
- **Package size:** 1,075.5 MB before the props, 1,469.0 MB after.
  - The props cook to 398.3 MB. That fits the 406 MB growth of the game's main data file (`.ucas`).
  - HANDOFF.md lists every prop's cooked size.
- **Pictures:** all taken.
  - The last retake shows the Grunt holding the revolver in its right hand. It is walking and turned away, and the Marksman's gun is hidden behind it, so only the test checks the Marksman's gun.
  - The lamp pictures confirm the glowing plate sits on the LED panel's face. That position was a guess before.
- **Frame times:** I can't tell you whether the props cost frame rate. The same room on the same package ran anywhere from 87 to 229 FPS, because [pc-c] is shared and its load decides the numbers. The handoff lists measuring on an idle PC as not checked.

**Left out for the prop lanes:** the wooden cable reel (broken texture on the reel ends), and the two plastic crates (blurred patches where letters were erased). The art was not touched. The old sandbag pile was swapped out as the jam thread asked.

**Calls for you, each marked `[taste: owner review]`**
- A scratch on the flatbed trolley could read as a "4".
- The crew stool blocks shots and sight like a solid box, where the chairs let them through. It could be made see-through like the chairs.
- The Marksman's shot starts 61 cm past its revolver's muzzle. I kept the shot point where it was, because moving it changes play.
- The lamp's barn doors cut dark bars across its lit face when seen from below.
- Cover props cook their textures at 2048. Dropping them to 1024 would save about 80 MB.

I also deleted `D:\UE\wt\props1_base`, the copy of the base commit I made for the before package.
